---------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m1p0t5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS DeskCount, OverrideBudget

Desks == 1 .. DeskCount
NextDesk(d) == IF d = DeskCount THEN 1 ELSE d + 1

VARIABLES token, deskMode, override, seizures, occupant
vars == <<token, deskMode, override, seizures, occupant>>

Modes == {"idle", "waiting", "settling", "settled"}

TypeOK ==
  /\ token \in Desks
  /\ deskMode \in [Desks -> Modes]
  /\ override \in {"clear", "engaged"}
  /\ seizures \in 0 .. OverrideBudget
  /\ occupant \in Desks \cup {0}

Init ==
  /\ token = 1
  /\ deskMode = [d \in Desks |-> "idle"]
  /\ override = "clear"
  /\ seizures = 0
  /\ occupant = 0

\* A desk raises its hand for the netting engine; it must then wait for the
\* circulating token before it may touch the engine.
RaiseBatch(d) ==
  /\ deskMode[d] \in {"idle", "settled"}
  /\ deskMode' = [deskMode EXCEPT ![d] = "waiting"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, override, seizures, occupant>>

\* The token is polite: it stays put while its desk still has business.
PassToken ==
  /\ deskMode[token] \notin {"waiting", "settling"}
  /\ token' = NextDesk(token)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<deskMode, override, seizures, occupant>>

OpenEngine(d) ==
  /\ token = d
  /\ deskMode[d] = "waiting"
  /\ override = "clear"
  /\ occupant = 0
  /\ occupant' = d
  /\ deskMode' = [deskMode EXCEPT ![d] = "settling"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, override, seizures>>

CloseEngine(d) ==
  /\ deskMode[d] = "settling"
  /\ occupant = d
  /\ occupant' = 0
  /\ deskMode' = [deskMode EXCEPT ![d] = "settled"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, override, seizures>>

\* Privileged override: the settlement supervisor may take the engine for a
\* manual correction, but only while no desk is inside it.
SupervisorSeize ==
  /\ override = "clear"
  /\ occupant = 0
  /\ seizures < OverrideBudget
  /\ override' = "engaged"
  /\ seizures' = seizures + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, deskMode, occupant>>

SupervisorRelease ==
  /\ override = "engaged"
  /\ override' = "clear"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, deskMode, seizures, occupant>>

Next ==
  \/ \E d \in Desks : RaiseBatch(d)
  \/ PassToken
  \/ \E d \in Desks : OpenEngine(d)
  \/ \E d \in Desks : CloseEngine(d)
  \/ SupervisorSeize
  \/ SupervisorRelease

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ SF_vars(PassToken)
  /\ WF_vars(\E d \in Desks : CloseEngine(d))
  /\ WF_vars(SupervisorRelease)
  /\ WF_vars(\E d \in Desks : OpenEngine(d))

\* A desk touching the netting engine must be the token holder and must not be
\* competing with an active supervisor override.
ExclusiveEngineUse ==
  \A d \in Desks :
    deskMode[d] = "settling" => (occupant = d /\ token = d /\ override = "clear")

\* The token keeps circulating and the override budget is finite, so a raised
\* batch cannot be held off forever.
EveryBatchEventuallySettles ==
  \A d \in Desks : (deskMode[d] = "waiting") ~> (deskMode[d] = "settled")
============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    DeskCount = 3
    OverrideBudget = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT ExclusiveEngineUse

PROPERTY EveryBatchEventuallySettles
nl:
A commercial bank runs its interbank settlement batches through a single netting engine that only one settlement desk may occupy at a time. The desks sit in a fixed ring, and a settlement token circulates around that ring: the token moves from a desk to its neighbour, wraps around at the last desk back to the first, and only the desk currently holding the token is allowed to open the engine. The token is polite: it is never passed on while the desk holding it still has a batch waiting or is in the middle of a settlement run.

A desk that has a batch to net raises it, which puts the desk into a waiting state. When the token reaches a waiting desk and the engine is free, that desk opens the engine and becomes the engine's occupant; when it has netted its batch it closes the engine, releasing it and marking the batch settled. A settled desk may later raise another batch.

The bank also allows a privileged override: the settlement supervisor may seize the engine directly to make a manual correction, bypassing the ring entirely. The supervisor may only seize the engine while nobody is inside it, and while the override is engaged no desk may open the engine. The supervisor eventually releases the engine, and the bank's operating rules cap how many manual seizures may happen in one batch window.

The full action set is: a desk raises a batch, the token is passed to the next desk in the ring, a waiting token-holding desk opens the engine, an occupying desk closes the engine, the supervisor seizes the engine under override, and the supervisor releases the engine.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any desk that is actively netting inside the engine is recorded as the engine's sole occupant, is the current holder of the settlement token, and is running while no supervisor override is engaged.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every desk that raises a batch and enters the waiting state eventually completes a settlement run on the netting engine.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m8p2t4 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cars, Sections, Dispatchers, MaxBerths

Free == 0
Handles == Dispatchers \cup {Free}

VARIABLES stabled, rolling, berths, lineKey, sectionKey
vars == <<stabled, rolling, berths, lineKey, sectionKey>>

Occupancy(s) == Cardinality(stabled[s])

TypeOK ==
  /\ stabled \in [Sections -> SUBSET Cars]
  /\ rolling \subseteq Cars
  /\ berths \in [Sections -> 1 .. MaxBerths]
  /\ lineKey \in Handles
  /\ sectionKey \in [Sections -> Handles]

Init ==
  /\ stabled = [s \in Sections |-> {}]
  /\ rolling = Cars
  /\ berths = [s \in Sections |-> 1]
  /\ lineKey = Free
  /\ sectionKey = [s \in Sections |-> Free]

\* Hierarchical interlocking: the coarse line key must be taken before any
\* fine-grained section key, and it is handed back once the section is held.
TakeLineKey(g) ==
  /\ lineKey = Free
  /\ lineKey' = g
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stabled, rolling, berths, sectionKey>>

TakeSectionKey(g, s) ==
  /\ lineKey = g
  /\ sectionKey[s] = Free
  /\ sectionKey' = [sectionKey EXCEPT ![s] = g]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stabled, rolling, berths, lineKey>>

DropLineKey(g) ==
  /\ lineKey = g
  /\ lineKey' = Free
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stabled, rolling, berths, sectionKey>>

DropSectionKey(g, s) ==
  /\ sectionKey[s] = g
  /\ sectionKey' = [sectionKey EXCEPT ![s] = Free]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stabled, rolling, berths, lineKey>>

\* A car leaving a stabling section becomes rolling stock on the running line;
\* it is removed from the section in the very same step it joins the line.
RollOut(g, s, c) ==
  /\ sectionKey[s] = g
  /\ c \in stabled[s]
  /\ stabled' = [stabled EXCEPT ![s] = stabled[s] \ {c}]
  /\ rolling' = rolling \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<berths, lineKey, sectionKey>>

RollIn(g, s, c) ==
  /\ sectionKey[s] = g
  /\ c \in rolling
  /\ Occupancy(s) < berths[s]
  /\ stabled' = [stabled EXCEPT ![s] = stabled[s] \cup {c}]
  /\ rolling' = rolling \ {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<berths, lineKey, sectionKey>>

\* Berth capacity is re-declared at runtime as engineering works open or close
\* stabling roads; it never moves a car, only the room available for cars.
Retune(s, k) ==
  /\ sectionKey[s] = Free
  /\ berths' = [berths EXCEPT ![s] = k]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stabled, rolling, lineKey, sectionKey>>

Next ==
  \/ \E g \in Dispatchers : TakeLineKey(g)
  \/ \E g \in Dispatchers, s \in Sections : TakeSectionKey(g, s)
  \/ \E g \in Dispatchers : DropLineKey(g)
  \/ \E g \in Dispatchers, s \in Sections : DropSectionKey(g, s)
  \/ \E g \in Dispatchers, s \in Sections, c \in Cars : RollOut(g, s, c)
  \/ \E g \in Dispatchers, s \in Sections, c \in Cars : RollIn(g, s, c)
  \/ \E s \in Sections, k \in 1 .. MaxBerths : Retune(s, k)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every car on the roster sits in exactly one place: one stabling section or
\* the running line. Nothing is duplicated into two sections and nothing is lost.
FleetIsConserved ==
  /\ rolling \cup (UNION {stabled[s] : s \in Sections}) = Cars
  /\ \A s \in Sections : stabled[s] \cap rolling = {}
  /\ \A s, t \in Sections : s # t => stabled[s] \cap stabled[t] = {}
===========================================================================
nl:
A subway operator divides its depot approach into stabling sections, each holding a limited number of berths, with a running line connecting them. Every railcar on the roster is either stabled in one of the sections or is rolling on the running line; the operator's rolling-stock register must always account for each car exactly once.

Movements are authorised through a two-level interlocking. A dispatcher must first take the coarse line key, which only one dispatcher may hold at a time. While holding the line key the dispatcher may take the fine-grained section key for a particular stabling section, and the line key is then handed back so another dispatcher can start its own sequence. A dispatcher may only shunt cars in a section whose section key it currently holds, and it drops the section key when finished.

Shunting a car out of a section removes it from that section's berths and puts it on the running line in the same movement. Shunting a car in takes it off the running line and places it in the section, which is only permitted while that section still has a free berth. Berth capacity is not fixed: engineering works open and close stabling roads, so the number of berths declared for a section is re-tuned at runtime, but only while nobody holds that section's key, and re-tuning never moves a car.

The full action set is: take the line key, take a section key while holding the line key, drop the line key, drop a section key, roll a car out of a section onto the running line, roll a car in from the running line into a section with a free berth, and re-tune a section's berth count.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The stabling sections and the running line always partition the full car roster, so every car is accounted for in exactly one location and no car is ever duplicated across two sections or lost from the register.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od5m2p3t3 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Slots, Players, Shards, Vacant

Ballots == {"unmarked", "accept", "refuse"}
Rounds == {"quiet", "polling", "landing"}

VARIABLES phase, offer, ballot, roster, reserved
vars == <<phase, offer, ballot, roster, reserved>>

AllVoted == \A n \in Shards : ballot[n] # "unmarked"
Unanimous == \A n \in Shards : ballot[n] = "accept"
FullyLanded == \A n \in Shards : roster[n][offer.slot] = offer.player

TypeOK ==
  /\ phase \in Rounds
  /\ offer \in [slot : Slots, player : Players]
  /\ ballot \in [Shards -> Ballots]
  /\ roster \in [Shards -> [Slots -> Players \cup {Vacant}]]
  /\ reserved \in [Shards -> SUBSET Slots]

Init ==
  /\ phase = "quiet"
  /\ offer \in [slot : Slots, player : Players]
  /\ ballot = [n \in Shards |-> "unmarked"]
  /\ roster = [n \in Shards |-> [k \in Slots |-> Vacant]]
  /\ reserved = [n \in Shards |-> {}]

OpenPoll(k, p) ==
  /\ phase = "quiet"
  /\ phase' = "polling"
  /\ offer' = [slot |-> k, player |-> p]
  /\ ballot' = [n \in Shards |-> "unmarked"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<roster, reserved>>

\* A shard accepts only if the seat is still empty in its own roster AND it has
\* not already promised that seat in an earlier round; accepting takes the hold.
CastBallot(n) ==
  /\ phase = "polling"
  /\ ballot[n] = "unmarked"
  /\ IF offer.slot \notin reserved[n] /\ roster[n][offer.slot] = Vacant
       THEN /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![n] = "accept"]
            /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![n] = reserved[n] \cup {offer.slot}]
       ELSE /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![n] = "refuse"]
            /\ UNCHANGED reserved
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, offer, roster>>

CallCommit ==
  /\ phase = "polling"
  /\ Unanimous
  /\ phase' = "landing"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<offer, ballot, roster, reserved>>

\* On a refusal the round is dropped and only the holds taken in this round are
\* given back, so an older promise on the same seat survives the rollback.
CallAbort ==
  /\ phase = "polling"
  /\ AllVoted
  /\ ~Unanimous
  /\ reserved' = [n \in Shards |->
        IF ballot[n] = "accept" THEN reserved[n] \ {offer.slot} ELSE reserved[n]]
  /\ phase' = "quiet"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<offer, ballot, roster>>

\* Shards are slow, not broken: each one writes the seat into its own roster
\* whenever it gets around to it, so rosters lag behind the commit decision.
LandSeat(n) ==
  /\ phase = "landing"
  /\ roster[n][offer.slot] = Vacant
  /\ roster' = [roster EXCEPT ![n][offer.slot] = offer.player]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, offer, ballot, reserved>>

ClosePoll ==
  /\ phase = "landing"
  /\ FullyLanded
  /\ phase' = "quiet"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<offer, ballot, roster, reserved>>

Next ==
  \/ \E k \in Slots, p \in Players : OpenPoll(k, p)
  \/ \E n \in Shards : CastBallot(n)
  \/ CallCommit
  \/ CallAbort
  \/ \E n \in Shards : LandSeat(n)
  \/ ClosePoll

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(\E n \in Shards : CastBallot(n))
  /\ WF_vars(CallCommit)
  /\ WF_vars(CallAbort)
  /\ WF_vars(\E n \in Shards : LandSeat(n))
  /\ WF_vars(ClosePoll)

\* Wherever a seat has been filled, every shard that has filled it names the
\* same player: one lobby seat is never sold to two different players.
NoSeatDoubleBooked ==
  \A k \in Slots, m, n \in Shards :
    (roster[m][k] # Vacant /\ roster[n][k] # Vacant) => roster[m][k] = roster[n][k]

\* Slow shards still finish, so a poll never hangs half-decided.
EveryPollEventuallySettles ==
  (phase = "polling") ~> (phase = "quiet")
==========================================================================
nl:
A multiplayer game's lobby matchmaker seats players into numbered lobby slots that are replicated across several shard servers. Each shard keeps its own roster mapping every slot to the player sitting there, or to vacant. Seating a player is agreed by a two-phase commit run by the matchmaker.

The matchmaker opens a poll by naming one slot and one player and clearing all previous ballots. Each shard then casts its ballot: it accepts only if that slot is still vacant in its own roster and it has not already promised the slot in an earlier round, and accepting takes a hold on the slot; otherwise it refuses. If every shard accepts, the matchmaker calls the commit and the round moves into landing. If all ballots are in and at least one is a refusal, the matchmaker aborts the round and gives back only the holds that were taken during this round, so a hold promised in an earlier round survives the rollback.

Shards in this deployment are slow but never failed. Once the commit is called, each shard writes the player into its own roster whenever it gets around to it, so for a while some rosters show the seat filled while others still show it vacant. The matchmaker closes the poll only once every shard has landed the seat, and only then can a new poll be opened.

The full action set is: open a poll for a slot and a player, a shard casts its accept-or-refuse ballot and takes a hold when it accepts, the matchmaker calls a commit on unanimous acceptance, the matchmaker aborts the round and returns this round's holds, a shard lands the committed seat into its own roster, and the matchmaker closes a fully landed poll.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever two shards both show a given lobby slot as filled, they name the same player, so no slot is ever allocated to two different players.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every poll the matchmaker opens eventually settles, either by aborting or by landing on every shard, so the matchmaker always returns to a quiet state ready for the next poll.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m9p0t2 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS RouteCrew, ContractCrew, Kiosks, MaxEpoch

Techs == RouteCrew \cup ContractCrew
Nobody == "nobody"
Duty == {"offshift", "onsite", "atvault"}

VARIABLES epoch, warrant, duty, vault, refilled
vars == <<epoch, warrant, duty, vault, refilled>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
  /\ warrant \in [Techs -> 0 .. MaxEpoch]
  /\ duty \in [Techs -> Duty]
  /\ vault \in Techs \cup {Nobody}
  /\ refilled \subseteq Kiosks

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ warrant = [t \in Techs |-> 0]
  /\ duty = [t \in Techs |-> "offshift"]
  /\ vault = Nobody
  /\ refilled = {}

\* Reconfiguration bumps the network epoch and hands the new epoch's warrant to
\* exactly one technician, drawn from either crew; every older warrant is stale.
Reconfigure(t) ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ vault = Nobody
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ warrant' = [warrant EXCEPT ![t] = epoch + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<duty, vault, refilled>>

ReportForShift(t) ==
  /\ duty[t] = "offshift"
  /\ duty' = [duty EXCEPT ![t] = "onsite"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, warrant, vault, refilled>>

StandDown(t) ==
  /\ duty[t] = "onsite"
  /\ duty' = [duty EXCEPT ![t] = "offshift"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, warrant, vault, refilled>>

\* Only a technician whose warrant carries the live epoch may open the shared
\* coin-float vault, and only while nobody else has it open.
OpenVault(t) ==
  /\ duty[t] = "onsite"
  /\ warrant[t] = epoch
  /\ vault = Nobody
  /\ vault' = t
  /\ duty' = [duty EXCEPT ![t] = "atvault"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, warrant, refilled>>

TopUpKiosk(t, k) ==
  /\ vault = t
  /\ duty[t] = "atvault"
  /\ k \notin refilled
  /\ refilled' = refilled \cup {k}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, warrant, duty, vault>>

SealVault(t) ==
  /\ vault = t
  /\ duty[t] = "atvault"
  /\ vault' = Nobody
  /\ duty' = [duty EXCEPT ![t] = "onsite"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, warrant, refilled>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Techs : Reconfigure(t)
  \/ \E t \in Techs : ReportForShift(t)
  \/ \E t \in Techs : StandDown(t)
  \/ \E t \in Techs : OpenVault(t)
  \/ \E t \in Techs, k \in Kiosks : TopUpKiosk(t, k)
  \/ \E t \in Techs : SealVault(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Anyone standing at the shared float vault is the recorded holder of it and is
\* working under a warrant stamped with the network's current epoch.
VaultHeldUnderLiveWarrant ==
  \A t \in Techs :
    duty[t] = "atvault" => (vault = t /\ warrant[t] = epoch)
===========================================================================
nl:
A regional vending operator runs a network of kiosks that are serviced by two independent crews: its own route crew and an outsourced contract crew. Both crews draw from the same single coin-float vault at the depot, and that vault is the critical resource: only one technician may have it open at any moment, no matter which crew they belong to.

Service rights are managed by epoch-numbered reconfiguration. The depot controller bumps the network epoch and, in the same step, stamps the new epoch number onto exactly one technician's warrant; every warrant issued in an earlier epoch immediately becomes stale. The controller only reconfigures while the vault is sealed, and the epoch counter runs up to a fixed ceiling for a service window.

A technician reports for shift to come on site and may stand down again to go off shift. A technician who is on site may open the shared vault only if the warrant they hold carries the network's current epoch and nobody else has the vault open. While standing at the vault a technician may top up a kiosk that has not yet been refilled in this window, drawing coins from the float. When finished, the technician seals the vault and returns to being merely on site.

The full action set is: reconfigure the network by bumping the epoch and warranting one technician, report for shift, stand down from shift, open the shared float vault under a current-epoch warrant, top up a not-yet-refilled kiosk while at the vault, and seal the vault.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any technician standing at the shared coin-float vault is recorded as its sole current holder and is working under a warrant stamped with the network's live epoch, so a stale-warranted or second technician can never be at the vault at the same time.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m7p0t4 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS CtrlA, CtrlB, CtrlC, FreeCell, MinLanes, MaxLanes, BalkLimit

Controllers == {CtrlA, CtrlB, CtrlC}
LaneRange == MinLanes .. MaxLanes

VARIABLES cell, stage, lanes, adopted, balks
vars == <<cell, stage, lanes, adopted, balks>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ cell \in Controllers \cup {FreeCell}
  /\ stage \in [Controllers -> {"resting", "queued", "holding"}]
  /\ lanes \in LaneRange
  /\ adopted \subseteq Controllers
  /\ balks \in 0 .. BalkLimit

Init ==
  /\ cell = FreeCell
  /\ stage = [c \in Controllers |-> "resting"]
  /\ lanes = MinLanes
  /\ adopted = Controllers
  /\ balks = 0

JoinQueue(c) ==
  /\ stage[c] = "resting"
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "queued"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cell, lanes, adopted, balks>>

\* The compare-and-swap: a queued controller writes its own id into the console
\* register, but only if the register still reads as free at that instant.
Swap(c) ==
  /\ stage[c] = "queued"
  /\ cell = FreeCell
  /\ cell' = c
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "holding"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lanes, adopted, balks>>

\* A losing compare-and-swap changes nothing but the backoff counter.
Balk(c) ==
  /\ stage[c] = "queued"
  /\ cell # FreeCell
  /\ balks < BalkLimit
  /\ balks' = balks + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cell, stage, lanes, adopted>>

\* Lane capacity is re-declared while the network runs; only the controller that
\* won the register may do it, and every machine must re-adopt the new figure.
Retune(c, k) ==
  /\ cell = c
  /\ stage[c] = "holding"
  /\ k # lanes
  /\ lanes' = k
  /\ adopted' = {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cell, stage, balks>>

Adopt(c) ==
  /\ c \notin adopted
  /\ adopted' = adopted \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cell, stage, lanes, balks>>

Unswap(c) ==
  /\ stage[c] = "holding"
  /\ cell' = FreeCell
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "resting"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lanes, adopted, balks>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Controllers : JoinQueue(c)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers : Swap(c)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers : Balk(c)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers, k \in LaneRange : Retune(c, k)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers : Adopt(c)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers : Unswap(c)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(\E c \in Controllers : Unswap(c))
  /\ SF_vars(Swap(CtrlA))
  /\ SF_vars(Swap(CtrlB))
  /\ SF_vars(Swap(CtrlC))

\* Whoever believes it is holding the planogram console is exactly the id
\* written in the register, so two controllers can never both be holding it.
ConsoleMatchesRegister ==
  \A c \in Controllers : stage[c] = "holding" => cell = c

\* Every holder eventually lets the register go, so a queued controller that
\* keeps retrying will win the swap sooner or later.
EveryQueuedControllerEventuallyHolds ==
  \A c \in Controllers : (stage[c] = "queued") ~> (stage[c] = "holding")
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    CtrlA = a
    CtrlB = b
    CtrlC = d
    FreeCell = free
    MinLanes = 2
    MaxLanes = 4
    BalkLimit = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT ConsoleMatchesRegister

PROPERTY EveryQueuedControllerEventuallyHolds
nl:
A chain of vending machines is administered by three route controllers who share one planogram console. The console is guarded by a single compare-and-swap register: the register either reads free or carries the id of exactly one controller, and a controller is entitled to work at the console only while the register carries its own id.

A resting controller that wants the console joins the queue. A queued controller then attempts the swap: it writes its own id into the register, but the write only takes effect if the register still reads free at that instant. If the register is already carrying someone else's id, the attempt balks: nothing changes except a backoff counter, and the chain permits only a limited number of balks in a service window.

The interesting work at the console is retuning capacity while the network runs: the controller currently holding the register re-declares how many dispensing lanes each machine should keep enabled, picking a new figure inside the chain's permitted lane range. Retuning marks every machine as needing to re-adopt the new figure except the controller that made the change, and machines then adopt the new lane figure one at a time. A holder finishes by clearing the register back to free and returning to rest.

The full action set is: a resting controller joins the queue, a queued controller wins the compare-and-swap and takes the console, a queued controller balks on a lost swap, the register holder retunes the network lane capacity, a machine adopts the current lane figure, and the holder clears the register.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every controller that believes it is holding the planogram console is exactly the id written in the compare-and-swap register, so two controllers can never both hold the console at once.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every controller that joins the queue eventually wins the compare-and-swap and holds the console.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m4p2t2 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS TotalSheets, JobSizes, DeskDepth, TrayDepth, DeferLimit

VARIABLES pool, deskQ, trayQ, printed, deferrals
vars == <<pool, deskQ, trayQ, printed, deferrals>>

RECURSIVE SheetsIn(_)
SheetsIn(q) == IF q = <<>> THEN 0 ELSE Head(q) + SheetsIn(Tail(q))

TypeOK ==
  /\ pool \in 0 .. TotalSheets
  /\ printed \in 0 .. TotalSheets
  /\ deferrals \in 0 .. DeferLimit
  /\ Len(deskQ) <= DeskDepth
  /\ Len(trayQ) <= TrayDepth

Init ==
  /\ pool = TotalSheets
  /\ deskQ = <<>>
  /\ trayQ = <<>>
  /\ printed = 0
  /\ deferrals = 0

\* Admitting a job onto a spooler moves its sheet allowance out of the shared
\* pool and into that spooler's queue; the sheets are not created there.
AdmitToDesk(sz) ==
  /\ Len(deskQ) < DeskDepth
  /\ pool >= sz
  /\ pool' = pool - sz
  /\ deskQ' = Append(deskQ, sz)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<trayQ, printed, deferrals>>

AdmitToTray(sz) ==
  /\ Len(trayQ) < TrayDepth
  /\ pool >= sz
  /\ pool' = pool - sz
  /\ trayQ' = Append(trayQ, sz)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<deskQ, printed, deferrals>>

\* Backpressure: a full queue refuses the job outright. No sheets move at all,
\* which is exactly why a refusal cannot disturb the ledger.
DeferJob ==
  /\ Len(deskQ) = DeskDepth \/ Len(trayQ) = TrayDepth
  /\ deferrals < DeferLimit
  /\ deferrals' = deferrals + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, deskQ, trayQ, printed>>

RunDeskHead ==
  /\ deskQ # <<>>
  /\ printed' = printed + Head(deskQ)
  /\ deskQ' = Tail(deskQ)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, trayQ, deferrals>>

RunTrayHead ==
  /\ trayQ # <<>>
  /\ printed' = printed + Head(trayQ)
  /\ trayQ' = Tail(trayQ)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, deskQ, deferrals>>

\* Guillotined misprints go back to the shared pool as blank stock.
ReclaimMisprint(sz) ==
  /\ printed >= sz
  /\ printed' = printed - sz
  /\ pool' = pool + sz
  /\ UNCHANGED <<deskQ, trayQ, deferrals>>

Next ==
  \/ \E sz \in JobSizes : AdmitToDesk(sz)
  \/ \E sz \in JobSizes : AdmitToTray(sz)
  \/ DeferJob
  \/ RunDeskHead
  \/ RunTrayHead
  \/ \E sz \in JobSizes : ReclaimMisprint(sz)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every sheet the shop started the day with is somewhere: unallocated in the
\* shared pool, committed to one of the two spool queues, or already printed.
SheetLedgerBalances ==
  pool + SheetsIn(deskQ) + SheetsIn(trayQ) + printed = TotalSheets
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    TotalSheets = 6
    JobSizes = {1, 2, 3}
    DeskDepth = 2
    TrayDepth = 2
    DeferLimit = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT SheetLedgerBalances
nl:
A print shop runs two independent spooler instances -- the walk-up desk spooler and the output-tray spooler -- and both of them draw blank stock from one shared paper pool. The pool starts the day holding the shop's entire sheet count, and the shop's ledger must always be able to say where every one of those sheets is.

Each spooler holds a bounded queue of accepted jobs, and each job carries the number of sheets it will consume. Admitting a job to a spooler is only allowed when that spooler's queue is below its depth limit and the shared pool still holds enough blank stock; admitting moves the job's sheet allowance out of the pool and into that spooler's queue in a single step. When a queue is at its depth limit the shop applies backpressure and defers the job instead: nothing is queued and no sheets move at all, only a deferral is recorded, and the shop tolerates a limited number of deferrals per shift.

Each spooler prints its queue head, which retires that job from the queue and adds its sheets to the printed total. Guillotined misprints are recycled: a batch of printed sheets is taken back out of the printed total and returned to the shared pool as blank stock.

The full action set is: admit a job of a given size to the desk spooler, admit a job of a given size to the tray spooler, defer a job under backpressure when a queue is full, print the head of the desk queue, print the head of the tray queue, and reclaim a batch of misprints back into the shared pool.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The sheets sitting unallocated in the shared pool, the sheets committed to the two spool queues, and the sheets already printed always add up to exactly the shop's starting sheet count, so no sheet is ever conjured up or lost between the two independent spoolers.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m5p0t2 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS NorthPress, SouthPress, Arbiters, Jobs, Unpledged, Unplated, MisfeedCap

Presses == {NorthPress, SouthPress}

VARIABLES pressState, ballot, platedBy, misfeeds, turnedAway
vars == <<pressState, ballot, platedBy, misfeeds, turnedAway>>

Pledged(p) == {a \in Arbiters : ballot[a] = p}
Uncommitted == {a \in Arbiters : ballot[a] = Unpledged}
HasQuorum(p) == 2 * Cardinality(Pledged(p)) > Cardinality(Arbiters)
QuorumHopeless(p) ==
  2 * (Cardinality(Pledged(p)) + Cardinality(Uncommitted)) <= Cardinality(Arbiters)

TypeOK ==
  /\ pressState \in [Presses -> {"idle", "canvassing", "mounted", "rebuffed"}]
  /\ ballot \in [Arbiters -> Presses \cup {Unpledged}]
  /\ platedBy \in [Jobs -> Presses \cup {Unplated}]
  /\ misfeeds \in 0 .. MisfeedCap
  /\ turnedAway \subseteq Presses

Init ==
  /\ pressState = [p \in Presses |-> "idle"]
  /\ ballot = [a \in Arbiters |-> Unpledged]
  /\ platedBy = [j \in Jobs |-> Unplated]
  /\ misfeeds = 0
  /\ turnedAway = {}

OpenCanvass(p) ==
  /\ pressState[p] = "idle"
  /\ pressState' = [pressState EXCEPT ![p] = "canvassing"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, platedBy, misfeeds, turnedAway>>

\* An arbiter pledges to at most one canvassing press, and defers to a branch
\* that was turned away last time so the same branch is not starved twice.
Pledge(a, p) ==
  /\ ballot[a] = Unpledged
  /\ pressState[p] = "canvassing"
  /\ ~ \E q \in Presses :
        /\ q # p
        /\ pressState[q] = "canvassing"
        /\ q \in turnedAway
        /\ p \notin turnedAway
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![a] = p]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pressState, platedBy, misfeeds, turnedAway>>

\* A strict majority of arbiters is what puts a branch on the plate-setter.
Mount(p) ==
  /\ pressState[p] = "canvassing"
  /\ HasQuorum(p)
  /\ pressState' = [pressState EXCEPT ![p] = "mounted"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, platedBy, misfeeds, turnedAway>>

Rebuff(p) ==
  /\ pressState[p] = "canvassing"
  /\ QuorumHopeless(p)
  /\ pressState' = [pressState EXCEPT ![p] = "rebuffed"]
  /\ ballot' = [a \in Arbiters |-> IF ballot[a] = p THEN Unpledged ELSE ballot[a]]
  /\ turnedAway' = turnedAway \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<platedBy, misfeeds>>

PlateJob(p, j) ==
  /\ pressState[p] = "mounted"
  /\ platedBy[j] = Unplated
  /\ platedBy' = [platedBy EXCEPT ![j] = p]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pressState, ballot, misfeeds, turnedAway>>

Misfeed ==
  /\ misfeeds < MisfeedCap
  /\ \E p \in Presses : pressState[p] = "mounted"
  /\ misfeeds' = misfeeds + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pressState, ballot, platedBy, turnedAway>>

StepDown(p) ==
  /\ pressState[p] \in {"mounted", "rebuffed"}
  /\ pressState' = [pressState EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
  /\ ballot' = [a \in Arbiters |-> IF ballot[a] = p THEN Unpledged ELSE ballot[a]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<platedBy, misfeeds, turnedAway>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Presses : OpenCanvass(p)
  \/ \E a \in Arbiters, p \in Presses : Pledge(a, p)
  \/ \E p \in Presses : Mount(p)
  \/ \E p \in Presses : Rebuff(p)
  \/ \E p \in Presses, j \in Jobs : PlateJob(p, j)
  \/ Misfeed
  \/ \E p \in Presses : StepDown(p)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ SF_vars(\E a \in Arbiters : Pledge(a, NorthPress))
  /\ SF_vars(\E a \in Arbiters : Pledge(a, SouthPress))
  /\ WF_vars(\E p \in Presses : Mount(p))
  /\ WF_vars(\E p \in Presses : Rebuff(p))
  /\ WF_vars(\E p \in Presses : StepDown(p))

\* A branch is only on the plate-setter while it is holding a strict majority
\* of the arbiters, and two majorities of one arbiter pool always overlap.
MountedOnlyWithQuorum ==
  \A p \in Presses : pressState[p] = "mounted" => HasQuorum(p)

\* No canvass hangs: with an odd arbiter pool a branch either wins a majority
\* or provably cannot, and either way it is told so.
EveryCanvassEventuallyDecided ==
  \A p \in Presses :
    (pressState[p] = "canvassing") ~> (pressState[p] \in {"mounted", "rebuffed"})
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NorthPress = north
    SouthPress = south
    Arbiters = {v1, v2, v3}
    Jobs = {j1, j2}
    Unpledged = unpledged
    Unplated = unplated
    MisfeedCap = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT MountedOnlyWithQuorum

PROPERTY EveryCanvassEventuallyDecided
nl:
A print shop runs two independent press branches, north and south, which share one plate-setter and one pool of scheduling arbiters. Only one branch may be mounted on the plate-setter at a time, and the shop decides who gets it by quorum voting rather than by a single dispatcher.

An idle branch opens a canvass. Each arbiter may pledge itself to at most one canvassing branch, and an arbiter that is still unpledged will defer to a branch that was turned away in an earlier round, so the same branch is not starved twice in a row. A branch that has collected a strict majority of the arbiter pool mounts the plate-setter. A branch whose pledges plus the remaining unpledged arbiters could never add up to a majority is rebuffed instead: it gives back the pledges it had collected and is recorded as having been turned away.

While mounted, a branch plates jobs from the shop's shared job list, marking each plated job with the branch that did it. The plate-setter occasionally misfeeds while a branch is mounted, which the shop logs up to a small daily limit. A branch that is mounted or rebuffed eventually steps down back to idle, releasing any pledges still held in its name.

The full action set is: a branch opens a canvass, an arbiter pledges to a canvassing branch, a branch with a majority mounts the plate-setter, a branch with no path to a majority is rebuffed and returns its pledges, a mounted branch plates a job, the plate-setter misfeeds, and a mounted or rebuffed branch steps down and releases its pledges.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A branch is on the plate-setter only while it holds a strict majority of the arbiter pool, and since two majorities of one pool always share an arbiter, the two branches can never be mounted at the same time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every canvass a branch opens is eventually decided, with the branch either mounting the plate-setter or being rebuffed.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od17m4p4t0 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Chutes, ChuteCapacity, LoopCapacity, CheckedBags

VARIABLES parked, enroute, loop, dead, waiting
vars == <<parked, enroute, loop, dead, waiting>>

Committed(c) == parked[c] + enroute[c]
Congested == \A c \in Chutes : Committed(c) = ChuteCapacity

TypeOK ==
  /\ parked \in [Chutes -> 0 .. ChuteCapacity]
  /\ enroute \in [Chutes -> 0 .. ChuteCapacity]
  /\ loop \in 0 .. LoopCapacity
  /\ dead \subseteq Chutes
  /\ waiting \in 0 .. CheckedBags

Init ==
  /\ parked = [c \in Chutes |-> 0]
  /\ enroute = [c \in Chutes |-> 0]
  /\ loop = 0
  /\ dead = {}
  /\ waiting = CheckedBags

\* The router reserves a chute slot the moment a bag leaves check-in, counting
\* the bag against that chute while it is still travelling on the belt.
Route(c) ==
  /\ waiting > 0
  /\ Committed(c) < ChuteCapacity
  /\ enroute' = [enroute EXCEPT ![c] = enroute[c] + 1]
  /\ waiting' = waiting - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<parked, loop, dead>>

\* Backpressure: with every chute fully committed the bag goes round the
\* recirculation loop instead of being pushed at a chute that has no room.
Recirculate ==
  /\ waiting > 0
  /\ Congested
  /\ loop < LoopCapacity
  /\ loop' = loop + 1
  /\ waiting' = waiting - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<parked, enroute, dead>>

Deliver(c) ==
  /\ enroute[c] > 0
  /\ enroute' = [enroute EXCEPT ![c] = enroute[c] - 1]
  /\ parked' = [parked EXCEPT ![c] = parked[c] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<loop, dead, waiting>>

\* A live handler pulls a bag off the chute and onto a cart.
Offload(c) ==
  /\ c \notin dead
  /\ parked[c] > 0
  /\ parked' = [parked EXCEPT ![c] = parked[c] - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<enroute, loop, dead, waiting>>

\* A handler can die quietly: nothing else changes and the router gets no
\* notification, so the reservation counters are the only defence left.
HandlerDies(c) ==
  /\ c \notin dead
  /\ dead' = dead \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<parked, enroute, loop, waiting>>

\* Ground staff eventually notice a chute that has stopped moving and clear it
\* by hand; that is the only way a dead handler's chute ever drains.
ManualClear(c) ==
  /\ c \in dead
  /\ parked[c] > 0
  /\ parked' = [parked EXCEPT ![c] = parked[c] - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<enroute, loop, dead, waiting>>

CheckIn ==
  /\ waiting < CheckedBags
  /\ waiting' = waiting + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<parked, enroute, loop, dead>>

Rejoin(c) ==
  /\ loop > 0
  /\ Committed(c) < ChuteCapacity
  /\ loop' = loop - 1
  /\ enroute' = [enroute EXCEPT ![c] = enroute[c] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<parked, dead, waiting>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Chutes : Route(c)
  \/ Recirculate
  \/ \E c \in Chutes : Deliver(c)
  \/ \E c \in Chutes : Offload(c)
  \/ \E c \in Chutes : HandlerDies(c)
  \/ \E c \in Chutes : ManualClear(c)
  \/ CheckIn
  \/ \E c \in Chutes : Rejoin(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bags already parked at a chute plus bags already committed to it on the belt
\* never exceed that chute's physical capacity, even when its handler is dead.
ChuteNeverOverCommitted ==
  \A c \in Chutes : parked[c] + enroute[c] <= ChuteCapacity
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Chutes = {ch1, ch2}
    ChuteCapacity = 2
    LoopCapacity = 2
    CheckedBags = 4

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT ChuteNeverOverCommitted
nl:
An airport baggage router feeds checked bags from the check-in hall down a belt to a small number of make-up chutes. Each chute holds a fixed number of bags before it physically jams, and a handler stands at each chute pulling bags off onto carts.

Because a bag spends time travelling on the belt after it has been aimed at a chute, the router counts a bag against its chute from the moment it is routed, not from the moment it lands. A bag is routed to a chute only when that chute's parked bags plus the bags already travelling towards it are below the chute's capacity. When every chute is fully committed the router applies backpressure and sends the bag round the recirculation loop instead; the loop itself holds only a limited number of bags. A bag travelling on the belt eventually lands and becomes a parked bag at its chute, and a bag on the recirculation loop can rejoin the belt towards any chute that still has room.

Handlers are not reliable. A handler can die quietly at any time: nothing else about the system changes and the router receives no notification at all, so from then on that chute is never drained again and the router's reservation counters are the only thing standing between the chute and an overflow.

Ground staff eventually notice a chute that has stopped moving and clear it by hand, which is the only way a dead handler's chute ever drains. Meanwhile passengers keep checking bags in at the hall, up to the terminal's registered bag count.

The full action set is: route a waiting bag to a chute with spare committed capacity, recirculate a waiting bag when all chutes are fully committed, land a travelling bag at its chute, a live handler offloads a parked bag, a handler dies silently, ground staff manually clear a bag from a dead handler's chute, a passenger checks another bag in, and a bag on the loop rejoins the belt towards a chute with room.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every chute, the bags parked at it plus the bags already committed to it on the belt never exceed that chute's capacity, even after its handler has died silently and stopped draining it.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od7m7p3t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Gangs, BoxA, BoxB, BoxC, Bays, EmptyBay, NoBox, NoBay

Boxes == {BoxA, BoxB, BoxC}

VARIABLES slotWord, berth, bid, gangStage, shipped
vars == <<slotWord, berth, bid, gangStage, shipped>>

NoBid == [box |-> NoBox, bay |-> NoBay]

TypeOK ==
  /\ slotWord \in [Bays -> Boxes \cup {EmptyBay}]
  /\ berth \in [Boxes -> Bays \cup {NoBay}]
  /\ bid \in [Gangs -> [box : Boxes \cup {NoBox}, bay : Bays \cup {NoBay}]]
  /\ gangStage \in [Gangs -> {"slack", "probing", "grounded"}]
  /\ shipped \subseteq Boxes

Init ==
  /\ slotWord = [y \in Bays |-> EmptyBay]
  /\ berth = [b \in Boxes |-> NoBay]
  /\ bid = [g \in Gangs |-> NoBid]
  /\ gangStage = [g \in Gangs |-> "slack"]
  /\ shipped = {}

\* A gang picks an ungrounded box and aims it at a bay; no two gangs may work
\* the same box, but they happily aim at the same bay out of the shared pool.
Pick(g, b, y) ==
  /\ gangStage[g] = "slack"
  /\ berth[b] = NoBay
  /\ \A h \in Gangs : bid[h].box # b
  /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT ![g] = [box |-> b, bay |-> y]]
  /\ gangStage' = [gangStage EXCEPT ![g] = "probing"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotWord, berth, shipped>>

\* The compare-and-swap on the bay word: the box id is written only if the word
\* still reads empty, and the yard book is updated in the very same step.
Swap(g) ==
  /\ gangStage[g] = "probing"
  /\ slotWord[bid[g].bay] = EmptyBay
  /\ slotWord' = [slotWord EXCEPT ![bid[g].bay] = bid[g].box]
  /\ berth' = [berth EXCEPT ![bid[g].box] = bid[g].bay]
  /\ gangStage' = [gangStage EXCEPT ![g] = "grounded"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bid, shipped>>

\* A lost swap: the word already carries somebody else's box, so the gang drops
\* the bid and will aim somewhere else.
Spin(g) ==
  /\ gangStage[g] = "probing"
  /\ slotWord[bid[g].bay] # EmptyBay
  /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT ![g] = NoBid]
  /\ gangStage' = [gangStage EXCEPT ![g] = "slack"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotWord, berth, shipped>>

Release(g) ==
  /\ gangStage[g] = "grounded"
  /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT ![g] = NoBid]
  /\ gangStage' = [gangStage EXCEPT ![g] = "slack"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotWord, berth, shipped>>

\* A straddle carrier works independently of the gangs and takes grounded boxes
\* out to the ship, clearing the bay word as it goes.
Ship(b) ==
  /\ berth[b] # NoBay
  /\ slotWord' = [slotWord EXCEPT ![berth[b]] = EmptyBay]
  /\ berth' = [berth EXCEPT ![b] = NoBay]
  /\ shipped' = shipped \cup {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bid, gangStage>>

Next ==
  \/ \E g \in Gangs, b \in Boxes, y \in Bays : Pick(g, b, y)
  \/ \E g \in Gangs : Swap(g)
  \/ \E g \in Gangs : Spin(g)
  \/ \E g \in Gangs : Release(g)
  \/ \E b \in Boxes : Ship(b)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(\E g \in Gangs : Swap(g))
  /\ WF_vars(Ship(BoxA))
  /\ WF_vars(Ship(BoxB))
  /\ WF_vars(Ship(BoxC))

\* The yard book and the bay words never disagree: if the book says a box is
\* grounded in a bay, that bay's word carries exactly that box and no other.
BookAgreesWithBayWord ==
  \A b \in Boxes : berth[b] # NoBay => slotWord[berth[b]] = b

\* Nothing is grounded forever; the carrier keeps clearing the yard.
EveryGroundedBoxEventuallyShips ==
  \A b \in Boxes : (berth[b] # NoBay) ~> (b \in shipped)
============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Gangs = {quay, rail}
    BoxA = x1
    BoxB = x2
    BoxC = x3
    Bays = {y1, y2}
    EmptyBay = emptybay
    NoBox = nobox
    NoBay = nobay

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT BookAgreesWithBayWord

PROPERTY EveryGroundedBoxEventuallyShips
nl:
A container terminal grounds boxes into a small pool of yard bays. Two independent crane gangs work that same pool: the quay gang landing boxes off the ship's side and the rail gang landing boxes off the trains. Each bay is guarded by a single word in the yard control system, which either reads empty or carries the id of exactly one box, and the terminal also keeps a yard book recording which bay each box is grounded in.

A slack gang picks a box that is not currently grounded and aims it at one of the bays; two gangs are never allowed to work the same box, though nothing stops them aiming at the same bay, since the bays are one shared pool. A probing gang then attempts the compare-and-swap: it writes the box id into the bay word, but the write only lands if the word still reads empty at that instant, and the yard book is updated in the very same step. If the word already carries someone else's box the gang's attempt spins: the bid is dropped and the gang goes slack again to aim elsewhere. A gang that has grounded its box releases the bid and goes slack.

A straddle carrier works independently of the crane gangs. It takes any grounded box out to the ship, clearing that bay's word back to empty and striking the box from the yard book; the box is then on the terminal's shipped list, and an emptied bay is free to be worked again.

The full action set is: a slack gang picks an ungrounded box and aims it at a bay, a probing gang wins the compare-and-swap and grounds its box, a probing gang spins on a lost swap and goes slack, a grounded gang releases its bid, and the straddle carrier ships a grounded box out and clears its bay.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever the yard book says a box is grounded in a bay, that bay's control word carries exactly that box, so one bay is never allocated to two different boxes by the two gangs.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every box that gets grounded in a bay is eventually taken out by the straddle carrier and shipped.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m9p4t0 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Depots, Fridges, RatedUnits, EpochCeiling

VARIABLES chilled, inbound, era, badge, silent
vars == <<chilled, inbound, era, badge, silent>>

Booked(f) == chilled[f] + Cardinality(inbound[f])
Current(d) == badge[d] = era
Live(d) == d \notin silent

TypeOK ==
  /\ chilled \in [Fridges -> 0 .. RatedUnits]
  /\ inbound \in [Fridges -> SUBSET Depots]
  /\ era \in 0 .. EpochCeiling
  /\ badge \in [Depots -> 0 .. EpochCeiling]
  /\ silent \subseteq Depots

Init ==
  /\ chilled = [f \in Fridges |-> 0]
  /\ inbound = [f \in Fridges |-> {}]
  /\ era = 0
  /\ badge = [d \in Depots |-> 0]
  /\ silent = {}

\* Reconfiguration stamps a new era on the network and re-badges one depot with
\* it; every other badge is now out of date and buys no write rights.
Rebadge(d) ==
  /\ era < EpochCeiling
  /\ era' = era + 1
  /\ badge' = [badge EXCEPT ![d] = era + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<chilled, inbound, silent>>

\* A booking counts against the fridge before the unit physically arrives, so
\* the rated capacity is compared against stock plus outstanding bookings.
BookSlot(d, f) ==
  /\ Current(d)
  /\ Live(d)
  /\ d \notin inbound[f]
  /\ Booked(f) < RatedUnits
  /\ inbound' = [inbound EXCEPT ![f] = inbound[f] \cup {d}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<chilled, era, badge, silent>>

LandUnit(d, f) ==
  /\ Current(d)
  /\ Live(d)
  /\ d \in inbound[f]
  /\ inbound' = [inbound EXCEPT ![f] = inbound[f] \ {d}]
  /\ chilled' = [chilled EXCEPT ![f] = chilled[f] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<era, badge, silent>>

IssueUnit(d, f) ==
  /\ Current(d)
  /\ Live(d)
  /\ chilled[f] > 0
  /\ chilled' = [chilled EXCEPT ![f] = chilled[f] - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inbound, era, badge, silent>>

\* A depot can go silent without saying so; its bookings stay on the fridges.
GoSilent(d) ==
  /\ Live(d)
  /\ silent' = silent \cup {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<chilled, inbound, era, badge>>

\* Only a booking left by a depot known to be silent may be swept off a fridge.
SweepStale(d, f) ==
  /\ d \in silent
  /\ d \in inbound[f]
  /\ inbound' = [inbound EXCEPT ![f] = inbound[f] \ {d}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<chilled, era, badge, silent>>

BringBack(d) ==
  /\ d \in silent
  /\ silent' = silent \ {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<chilled, inbound, era, badge>>

Next ==
  \/ \E d \in Depots : Rebadge(d)
  \/ \E d \in Depots, f \in Fridges : BookSlot(d, f)
  \/ \E d \in Depots, f \in Fridges : LandUnit(d, f)
  \/ \E d \in Depots, f \in Fridges : IssueUnit(d, f)
  \/ \E d \in Depots : GoSilent(d)
  \/ \E d \in Depots, f \in Fridges : SweepStale(d, f)
  \/ \E d \in Depots : BringBack(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Units already chilled in a fridge plus units booked into it never exceed the
\* fridge's rated capacity, however many eras pass or depots fall silent.
FridgeNeverOverbooked ==
  \A f \in Fridges : chilled[f] + Cardinality(inbound[f]) <= RatedUnits
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Depots = {d1, d2}
    Fridges = {f1, f2}
    RatedUnits = 2
    EpochCeiling = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT FridgeNeverOverbooked
nl:
A regional blood bank tracks red-cell units across a set of chill fridges, each with a rated capacity in units. Collection depots write into that inventory, and write rights are handed out by epoch-numbered reconfiguration: the controller stamps a new era on the network and re-badges exactly one depot with the new era number, which immediately makes every other depot's badge out of date. Only a depot whose badge carries the current era may touch the inventory, and the era counter runs up to a fixed ceiling.

Booking is done ahead of the physical delivery. A current-era depot books a slot on a fridge, and that booking counts against the fridge's rated capacity from the moment it is made, even though the unit is still in transit; a depot holds at most one outstanding booking per fridge. When the unit arrives the depot lands it, which turns the booking into chilled stock. A current-era depot may also issue a chilled unit out to a hospital, which frees stock.

Depots are not reliable. A depot can go silent at any time without announcing it, and its outstanding bookings simply stay on the fridges holding capacity. The bank's housekeeping may sweep a booking off a fridge only once the depot that made it is known to be silent, and a silent depot may later be brought back into service.

The full action set is: re-badge one depot with a new era, a current-era live depot books a slot on a fridge, a current-era live depot lands a booked unit into chilled stock, a current-era live depot issues a chilled unit out, a depot goes silent, housekeeping sweeps a silent depot's stale booking off a fridge, and a silent depot is brought back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every fridge, the units already chilled in it plus the units booked into it never exceed that fridge's rated capacity, no matter how many eras pass or how many depots fall silent holding bookings.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m0p4t5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS DeskOne, DeskTwo, Tickets, ExposureCap, StampSpan, RetryCap

Desks == {DeskOne, DeskTwo}
Stamps == 0 .. (StampSpan - 1)
Blank == [stamp |-> 0, ticket |-> 0]

VARIABLES exposure, stamp, draft, deskPhase, retries
vars == <<exposure, stamp, draft, deskPhase, retries>>

Bump(v) == (v + 1) % StampSpan
Fits(d) == exposure + draft[d].ticket <= ExposureCap
StillFresh(d) == draft[d].stamp = stamp

TypeOK ==
  /\ exposure \in 0 .. ExposureCap
  /\ stamp \in Stamps
  /\ draft \in [Desks -> [stamp : Stamps, ticket : Tickets \cup {0}]]
  /\ deskPhase \in [Desks -> {"clear", "drafted"}]
  /\ retries \in 0 .. RetryCap

Init ==
  /\ exposure = 0
  /\ stamp = 0
  /\ draft = [d \in Desks |-> Blank]
  /\ deskPhase = [d \in Desks |-> "clear"]
  /\ retries = 0

\* Optimistic read: the desk takes a snapshot of the batch stamp along with the
\* ticket value it wants to add. Nothing is locked while it prepares.
TakeDraft(d, t) ==
  /\ deskPhase[d] = "clear"
  /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![d] = [stamp |-> stamp, ticket |-> t]]
  /\ deskPhase' = [deskPhase EXCEPT ![d] = "drafted"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<exposure, stamp, retries>>

\* Validate-and-write: the draft lands only if the batch stamp has not moved
\* since the snapshot AND the new exposure still fits under the cap.
Post(d) ==
  /\ deskPhase[d] = "drafted"
  /\ StillFresh(d)
  /\ Fits(d)
  /\ exposure' = exposure + draft[d].ticket
  /\ stamp' = Bump(stamp)
  /\ deskPhase' = [deskPhase EXCEPT ![d] = "clear"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<draft, retries>>

\* The mirror image of Post: a draft that is stale or no longer fits is dropped.
Drop(d) ==
  /\ deskPhase[d] = "drafted"
  /\ ~(StillFresh(d) /\ Fits(d))
  /\ deskPhase' = [deskPhase EXCEPT ![d] = "clear"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<exposure, stamp, draft, retries>>

Resolve(d) == Post(d) \/ Drop(d)

CountRetry(d) ==
  /\ deskPhase[d] = "drafted"
  /\ ~StillFresh(d)
  /\ retries < RetryCap
  /\ retries' = retries + 1
  /\ deskPhase' = [deskPhase EXCEPT ![d] = "clear"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<exposure, stamp, draft>>

\* Privileged override: the treasury officer writes straight into the batch
\* without a snapshot, but is still held to the same exposure cap.
OfficerPost(t) ==
  /\ exposure + t <= ExposureCap
  /\ exposure' = exposure + t
  /\ stamp' = Bump(stamp)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<draft, deskPhase, retries>>

OfficerUnwind(t) ==
  /\ exposure >= t
  /\ exposure' = exposure - t
  /\ stamp' = Bump(stamp)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<draft, deskPhase, retries>>

Next ==
  \/ \E d \in Desks, t \in Tickets : TakeDraft(d, t)
  \/ \E d \in Desks : Resolve(d)
  \/ \E d \in Desks : CountRetry(d)
  \/ \E t \in Tickets : OfficerPost(t)
  \/ \E t \in Tickets : OfficerUnwind(t)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(Resolve(DeskOne))
  /\ WF_vars(Resolve(DeskTwo))

\* The netted exposure of the settlement batch never rises above the cap the
\* bank has posted, whichever route the ticket came in by.
ExposureStaysUnderCap == exposure <= ExposureCap

\* Optimistic posting never spins forever: a drafted desk always ends up back
\* in the clear, whether its write landed or was thrown away.
EveryDraftEventuallyResolves ==
  \A d \in Desks : (deskPhase[d] = "drafted") ~> (deskPhase[d] = "clear")
============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    DeskOne = alpha
    DeskTwo = beta
    Tickets = {1, 2}
    ExposureCap = 3
    StampSpan = 3
    RetryCap = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT ExposureStaysUnderCap

PROPERTY EveryDraftEventuallyResolves
nl:
A bank assembles its interbank settlement batch under a posted exposure cap: the netted value of the batch may never rise above that cap. Two settlement desks feed the batch, and they do so optimistically rather than by locking it.

A clear desk takes a draft: it snapshots the batch's current stamp together with the ticket value it wants to add, and nothing is locked while it prepares the paperwork. To post the draft the desk validates and writes in one step: the write only lands if the batch stamp has not moved since the snapshot and the resulting exposure still fits under the cap, and a successful post advances the stamp. A drafted desk whose snapshot has gone stale, or whose ticket no longer fits under the cap, drops the draft and goes back to clear. A desk that finds its snapshot stale may instead record a retry, which also returns it to clear; the bank counts retries up to a fixed limit per batch window.

There is a privileged override. The treasury officer may post a ticket straight into the batch without taking a snapshot at all, and may also unwind value out of the batch. Both officer actions advance the batch stamp, invalidating every outstanding desk snapshot, but the officer is held to exactly the same exposure cap as the desks.

The full action set is: a clear desk takes a draft of a ticket, a drafted desk posts it after a successful validate, a drafted desk drops a stale or oversized draft, a drafted desk records a retry on a stale snapshot, the treasury officer posts a ticket under override, and the treasury officer unwinds value out of the batch.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The netted exposure of the settlement batch never rises above the bank's posted exposure cap, whether the value arrived through an optimistic desk post or through the treasury officer's override.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every desk that has taken a draft eventually returns to the clear state, so an optimistic attempt never spins forever undecided.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m6p6t1 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Depots, Nobody, TermSpan, LeaseTicks, ShelfCap, DispatchCap

Terms == 0 .. (TermSpan - 1)
Notes == [author : Depots, term : Terms]

VARIABLES term, lease, net, shelf, dispatched
vars == <<term, lease, net, shelf, dispatched>>

LeaseLive == lease.ttl > 0

TypeOK ==
  /\ term \in Terms
  /\ lease \in [holder : Depots \cup {Nobody}, ttl : 0 .. LeaseTicks]
  /\ net \subseteq Notes
  /\ shelf \in 0 .. ShelfCap
  /\ dispatched \in 0 .. DispatchCap

Init ==
  /\ term = 0
  /\ lease = [holder |-> Nobody, ttl |-> 0]
  /\ net = {}
  /\ shelf = 0
  /\ dispatched = 0

\* Time only ever eats into the lease; a lease is never extended in place.
Tick ==
  /\ LeaseLive
  /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT !.ttl = lease.ttl - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, net, shelf, dispatched>>

\* A fresh lease may only be cut once the old one has run out. Term numbers come
\* from a small recycled pool, so the tracker fences the network by throwing away
\* any queued note already stamped with the term it is about to reissue.
CutLease(d) ==
  /\ ~LeaseLive
  /\ term' = (term + 1) % TermSpan
  /\ lease' = [holder |-> d, ttl |-> LeaseTicks]
  /\ net' = {m \in net : m.term # (term + 1) % TermSpan}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, dispatched>>

\* Only the depot currently holding a live lease may put a note on the network,
\* and the note carries the term it was written under.
PostNote(d) ==
  /\ LeaseLive
  /\ lease.holder = d
  /\ net' = net \cup {[author |-> d, term |-> term]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, lease, shelf, dispatched>>

\* Notes arrive in any order; the tracker applies one only if it still carries
\* the live term and the lease behind it has not run out.
ApplyNote(m) ==
  /\ m \in net
  /\ m.term = term
  /\ LeaseLive
  /\ shelf < ShelfCap
  /\ shelf' = shelf + 1
  /\ net' = net \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, lease, dispatched>>

BinNote(m) ==
  /\ m \in net
  /\ (m.term # term \/ ~LeaseLive)
  /\ net' = net \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, lease, shelf, dispatched>>

IssueUnit ==
  /\ shelf > 0
  /\ dispatched < DispatchCap
  /\ shelf' = shelf - 1
  /\ dispatched' = dispatched + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, lease, net>>

Next ==
  \/ Tick
  \/ \E d \in Depots : CutLease(d)
  \/ \E d \in Depots : PostNote(d)
  \/ \E m \in Notes : ApplyNote(m)
  \/ \E m \in Notes : BinNote(m)
  \/ IssueUnit

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Anything still sitting on the reordering network that could still be applied
\* -- that is, anything stamped with the live term -- was written by the depot
\* that currently holds the lease. A lapsed depot's note can never masquerade.
OnlyLeaseHolderNotesAreLandable ==
  \A m \in net : m.term = term => m.author = lease.holder
===========================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Depots = {d1, d2}
    Nobody = nobody
    TermSpan = 3
    LeaseTicks = 2
    ShelfCap = 3
    DispatchCap = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT OnlyLeaseHolderNotesAreLandable
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker accepts stock notes from collection depots, but only from the depot that currently holds the write lease. A lease is cut for a fixed number of ticks and simply runs down; it is never extended in place, and a new lease may only be cut once the previous one has run out. Each lease carries a term number, and term numbers are drawn from a small recycled pool, so when the tracker cuts a lease it also throws away any note already queued on the network that bears the term it is about to reissue.

The network between the depots and the tracker does not preserve order. A depot holding a live lease posts a note stamped with the term it wrote under, and that note then sits on the network until the tracker gets to it, which may be long after other notes posted later. When the tracker picks a note up it applies it to the shelf count only if the note still carries the live term and the lease behind it has not run out; otherwise the note is binned. The tracker also issues units off the shelf to hospitals, up to a daily dispatch limit.

The full action set is: a tick of the clock runs a live lease down, the tracker cuts a fresh lease to a depot and fences the network of that term, the lease-holding depot posts a note, the tracker applies a note that still carries the live term under a live lease, the tracker bins a note that is stale or whose lease has lapsed, and the tracker issues a unit off the shelf.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every note still sitting on the reordering network that could still be applied -- that is, every note stamped with the live term -- was written by the depot that currently holds the lease, so a depot whose lease has lapsed can never have a queued note masquerade as a current one.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m5p6t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Relays, ShedSizes, Headrooms, GenCeiling

Gens == 0 .. GenCeiling
Endorsements == [relay : Relays, gen : Gens]

VARIABLES gridGen, headroom, motion, tally, relayGen
vars == <<gridGen, headroom, motion, tally, relayGen>>

Quorum == 2 * Cardinality(tally) > Cardinality(Relays)
Workable == motion.gen = gridGen /\ motion.shed <= headroom

TypeOK ==
  /\ gridGen \in Gens
  /\ headroom \in Headrooms
  /\ motion \in [gen : Gens, shed : ShedSizes, book : {"none", "open", "carried", "dropped"}]
  /\ tally \subseteq Endorsements
  /\ relayGen \in [Relays -> Gens]

Init ==
  /\ gridGen = 0
  /\ headroom = 2
  /\ motion = [gen |-> 0, shed |-> 1, book |-> "none"]
  /\ tally = {}
  /\ relayGen = [r \in Relays |-> 0]

\* Available headroom is re-declared while the grid runs; every re-declaration
\* advances the grid generation, which is what makes old credentials stale.
Retune(h) ==
  /\ gridGen < GenCeiling
  /\ headroom' = h
  /\ gridGen' = gridGen + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<motion, tally, relayGen>>

CatchUp(r) ==
  /\ relayGen[r] # gridGen
  /\ relayGen' = [relayGen EXCEPT ![r] = gridGen]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<gridGen, headroom, motion, tally>>

TableMotion(s) ==
  /\ motion.book = "none"
  /\ motion' = [gen |-> gridGen, shed |-> s, book |-> "open"]
  /\ tally' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<gridGen, headroom, relayGen>>

\* A relay may only endorse a motion raised under the generation it is itself
\* running, and its endorsement is filed with that generation stamped on it.
Endorse(r) ==
  /\ motion.book = "open"
  /\ relayGen[r] = motion.gen
  /\ ~ \E e \in tally : e.relay = r
  /\ tally' = tally \cup {[relay |-> r, gen |-> relayGen[r]]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<gridGen, headroom, motion, relayGen>>

\* A strict majority of relays carries the motion and the load is shed.
Carry ==
  /\ motion.book = "open"
  /\ Quorum
  /\ Workable
  /\ motion' = [motion EXCEPT !.book = "carried"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<gridGen, headroom, tally, relayGen>>

\* A motion whose generation has been overtaken, or whose shed no longer fits
\* the re-declared headroom, is dropped rather than executed.
DropMotion ==
  /\ motion.book = "open"
  /\ ~Workable
  /\ motion' = [motion EXCEPT !.book = "dropped"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<gridGen, headroom, tally, relayGen>>

CloseBook ==
  /\ motion.book \in {"carried", "dropped"}
  /\ motion' = [motion EXCEPT !.book = "none"]
  /\ tally' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<gridGen, headroom, relayGen>>

Next ==
  \/ \E h \in Headrooms : Retune(h)
  \/ \E r \in Relays : CatchUp(r)
  \/ \E s \in ShedSizes : TableMotion(s)
  \/ \E r \in Relays : Endorse(r)
  \/ Carry
  \/ DropMotion
  \/ CloseBook

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(\E r \in Relays : CatchUp(r))
  /\ WF_vars(\E r \in Relays : Endorse(r))
  /\ WF_vars(Carry)
  /\ WF_vars(DropMotion)

\* No motion is left on the table: it is carried by a live quorum or dropped.
EveryMotionEventuallyDecided ==
  (motion.book = "open") ~> (motion.book \in {"carried", "dropped"})

\* Every endorsement counted towards the quorum was filed under the very
\* generation the motion was raised in, so a relay running an overtaken
\* credential can never contribute to carrying a shed command.
NoStaleEndorsementInTally ==
  \A e \in tally : e.gen = motion.gen
============================================================================
nl:
A power-grid load shedder decides each shed command by quorum voting among its protection relays rather than by a single controller. The grid publishes how much headroom is currently available, and that headroom is re-declared while the grid is running as plant comes on and off bars. Every re-declaration advances the grid's generation number, and a relay's credential is only current while the generation it is running matches the grid's. A relay that has fallen behind catches up by adopting the grid's current generation.

The control room tables a motion naming how much load to shed; the motion records the generation it was raised under and opens the endorsement book. A relay may endorse an open motion only if the generation it is itself running matches the generation the motion was raised under, it may endorse a motion only once, and its endorsement is filed with that generation stamped on it. A motion endorsed by a strict majority of relays is carried and the load is shed, provided the motion was raised under the grid's current generation and its shed still fits inside the declared headroom. A motion whose generation has been overtaken by a re-declaration, or whose shed no longer fits the new headroom, is dropped rather than executed. Once a motion has been carried or dropped the book is closed and the tally cleared.

The full action set is: re-declare the available headroom and advance the generation, a lagging relay catches up to the current generation, the control room tables a motion, a relay endorses an open motion of its own generation, a majority-endorsed workable motion is carried, an overtaken or oversized motion is dropped, and the book is closed after a decision.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every endorsement counted in a motion's tally was filed under the very generation that motion was raised in, so a relay running an overtaken credential can never contribute to carrying a shed command.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every motion the control room tables is eventually decided, being either carried by a live quorum or dropped as overtaken.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od7m6p4t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cranes, Stacks, Idle, LeaseTicks, TierChoices, QuayCap

VARIABLES tiers, pledged, tierLimit, tenancy, quay
vars == <<tiers, pledged, tierLimit, tenancy, quay>>

Loading(s) == tiers[s] + pledged[s]
Tenant(c, s) == tenancy[s].holder = c /\ tenancy[s].ticks > 0

TypeOK ==
  /\ tiers \in [Stacks -> 0 .. QuayCap]
  /\ pledged \in [Stacks -> 0 .. QuayCap]
  /\ tierLimit \in [Stacks -> TierChoices]
  /\ tenancy \in [Stacks -> [holder : Cranes \cup {Idle}, ticks : 0 .. LeaseTicks]]
  /\ quay \in 0 .. QuayCap

Init ==
  /\ tiers = [s \in Stacks |-> 0]
  /\ pledged = [s \in Stacks |-> 0]
  /\ tierLimit = [s \in Stacks |-> 1]
  /\ tenancy = [s \in Stacks |-> [holder |-> Idle, ticks |-> 0]]
  /\ quay = QuayCap

\* Leases only ever run down. A stack whose lease has run out belongs to nobody.
Tick ==
  /\ \E s \in Stacks : tenancy[s].ticks > 0
  /\ tenancy' = [s \in Stacks |->
        IF tenancy[s].ticks > 0
          THEN [tenancy[s] EXCEPT !.ticks = tenancy[s].ticks - 1]
          ELSE tenancy[s]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tiers, pledged, tierLimit, quay>>

TakeStack(c, s) ==
  /\ tenancy[s].ticks = 0
  /\ tenancy' = [tenancy EXCEPT ![s] = [holder |-> c, ticks |-> LeaseTicks]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tiers, pledged, tierLimit, quay>>

\* A pledge books a tier before the box physically arrives, so a stack's load is
\* what is already standing on it plus what its tenant has promised to land.
Pledge(c, s) ==
  /\ Tenant(c, s)
  /\ quay > 0
  /\ Loading(s) < tierLimit[s]
  /\ pledged' = [pledged EXCEPT ![s] = pledged[s] + 1]
  /\ quay' = quay - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tiers, tierLimit, tenancy>>

Land(c, s) ==
  /\ Tenant(c, s)
  /\ pledged[s] > 0
  /\ pledged' = [pledged EXCEPT ![s] = pledged[s] - 1]
  /\ tiers' = [tiers EXCEPT ![s] = tiers[s] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tierLimit, tenancy, quay>>

\* When a lease lapses its unlanded pledges are voided and the boxes go back to
\* the quay, which is what keeps a lapsed tenant from squatting on tiers.
VoidPledge(s) ==
  /\ tenancy[s].ticks = 0
  /\ pledged[s] > 0
  /\ pledged' = [pledged EXCEPT ![s] = pledged[s] - 1]
  /\ quay' = quay + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tiers, tierLimit, tenancy>>

\* The yard re-declares a stack's tier limit while work is going on, but never
\* below what is already standing plus what is already pledged onto it.
Relimit(s, k) ==
  /\ k >= Loading(s)
  /\ tierLimit' = [tierLimit EXCEPT ![s] = k]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tiers, pledged, tenancy, quay>>

Strip(s) ==
  /\ tiers[s] > 0
  /\ tiers' = [tiers EXCEPT ![s] = tiers[s] - 1]
  /\ quay' = quay + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pledged, tierLimit, tenancy>>

Next ==
  \/ Tick
  \/ \E c \in Cranes, s \in Stacks : TakeStack(c, s)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes, s \in Stacks : Pledge(c, s)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes, s \in Stacks : Land(c, s)
  \/ \E s \in Stacks : VoidPledge(s)
  \/ \E s \in Stacks, k \in TierChoices : Relimit(s, k)
  \/ \E s \in Stacks : Strip(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Boxes already standing on a stack plus boxes pledged onto it never exceed the
\* tier limit currently declared for that stack, across lease turnover and
\* re-declarations of the limit itself.
StackNeverOverLoaded ==
  \A s \in Stacks : tiers[s] + pledged[s] <= tierLimit[s]
============================================================================
nl:
A container-ship crane yard stacks boxes into ground slots, and each slot has a declared tier limit -- the number of boxes that may stand on it. Ground conditions and reefer plugs change during a shift, so the yard re-declares a stack's tier limit while work is going on; a re-declaration may raise the limit freely but may never set it below what is already standing on the stack plus what has already been pledged onto it.

Stacks are worked under leases. A crane takes a lease on a stack that currently belongs to nobody, and that lease is granted for a fixed number of ticks. Ticks only ever run leases down; a lease is never extended, and once its ticks reach zero the stack belongs to nobody again.

Only the crane holding a live lease on a stack may work it. It first pledges a tier: a box is taken off the quay and booked against the stack before it physically arrives, so a stack's load is what is standing on it plus what its tenant has promised to land. The tenant then lands a pledged box, turning the pledge into a standing tier. If a lease lapses with pledges still outstanding, those pledges are voided and the boxes go back to the quay, which is what stops a lapsed tenant from squatting on tiers it will never fill. Any stack may also be stripped, taking a standing box back to the quay.

The full action set is: a tick runs live leases down, a crane takes a lease on an unleased stack, a live tenant pledges a tier and pulls a box off the quay, a live tenant lands a pledged box, a lapsed lease's pledge is voided back to the quay, the yard re-declares a stack's tier limit no lower than its current load, and a stack is stripped of a standing box.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every stack, the boxes already standing on it plus the boxes pledged onto it never exceed the tier limit currently declared for that stack, across lease turnover and re-declarations of the limit itself.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od8m3p5t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Registrars, Students, Vacant, TermCeiling, SeatChoices, Fee, ChargeCeiling

VARIABLES reign, waitlist, sealed, charged, seatCap
vars == <<reign, waitlist, sealed, charged, seatCap>>

Seated == Cardinality(sealed)

TypeOK ==
  /\ reign \in [chair : Registrars \cup {Vacant}, term : 0 .. TermCeiling]
  /\ waitlist \subseteq Students
  /\ sealed \subseteq Students
  /\ charged \in [Students -> 0 .. ChargeCeiling]
  /\ seatCap \in SeatChoices

Init ==
  /\ reign = [chair |-> Vacant, term |-> 0]
  /\ waitlist = {}
  /\ sealed = {}
  /\ charged = [s \in Students |-> 0]
  /\ seatCap = 1

\* A new registrar takes the chair in a strictly higher term; failover is just
\* the chair falling vacant, which no student's sealed record depends on.
TakeChair(r) ==
  /\ reign.term < TermCeiling
  /\ reign.chair # r
  /\ reign' = [chair |-> r, term |-> reign.term + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waitlist, sealed, charged, seatCap>>

ChairFalls ==
  /\ reign.chair # Vacant
  /\ reign' = [reign EXCEPT !.chair = Vacant]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waitlist, sealed, charged, seatCap>>

Apply(s) ==
  /\ s \notin waitlist
  /\ s \notin sealed
  /\ waitlist' = waitlist \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reign, sealed, charged, seatCap>>

\* Sealing a registration is the irreversible step: the seat is committed and
\* the tuition fee is posted. The student leaves the waitlist in the same step,
\* which is the only thing stopping a second chair from sealing them again.
Seal(s) ==
  /\ reign.chair # Vacant
  /\ s \in waitlist
  /\ Seated < seatCap
  /\ waitlist' = waitlist \ {s}
  /\ sealed' = sealed \cup {s}
  /\ charged' = [charged EXCEPT ![s] = charged[s] + Fee]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reign, seatCap>>

Withdraw(s) ==
  /\ s \in waitlist
  /\ waitlist' = waitlist \ {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reign, sealed, charged, seatCap>>

\* Room bookings move during registration week, so the seat cap is re-declared
\* at runtime; it is never set below the number of seats already sealed.
Recap(k) ==
  /\ k >= Seated
  /\ seatCap' = k
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reign, waitlist, sealed, charged>>

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Registrars : TakeChair(r)
  \/ ChairFalls
  \/ \E s \in Students : Apply(s)
  \/ \E s \in Students : Seal(s)
  \/ \E s \in Students : Withdraw(s)
  \/ \E k \in SeatChoices : Recap(k)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A student whose registration has been sealed is off the waitlist and carries
\* exactly one tuition fee, so no failover of the registrar chair can post the
\* irreversible charge a second time.
SealedStudentsBilledOnce ==
  \A s \in Students :
    s \in sealed => (s \notin waitlist /\ charged[s] = Fee)
============================================================================
nl:
A university course-registration system is run by a set of registrar processes, one of which holds the chair at any time. A registrar takes the chair only in a strictly higher term than the one currently recorded, and failover is modelled directly: the chair can simply fall vacant, after which some registrar takes it again in a higher term. The system runs for a bounded number of terms per registration week.

Students apply to a course, which puts them on its waitlist. Sealing a registration is the irreversible step: the seat is committed and the tuition fee is posted to the student's account, and there is no unseal. Only a registrar holding the chair may seal, and only while the number of seats already sealed is below the course's declared cap. Sealing takes the student off the waitlist in the very same step, which is the only thing that stops a later chair from sealing the same student a second time. A student who has not been sealed may withdraw from the waitlist.

Room bookings move around during registration week, so the seat cap is re-declared at runtime as lecture halls are swapped; the cap may be raised or lowered but is never set below the number of seats already sealed.

The full action set is: a registrar takes the chair in a higher term, the chair falls vacant, a student applies to the waitlist, the chair seals a waitlisted student's registration and posts the fee, a waitlisted student withdraws, and the seat cap is re-declared at runtime.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every student whose registration has been sealed is off the waitlist and carries exactly one tuition fee on their account, so no failover of the registrar chair can post the irreversible charge a second time.
