---------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m3p5t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Supervisors, Vehicles, Unmanned, TermTop, BeltPitches, LineCap

ExitPitch == BeltPitches - 1

VARIABLES chair, onBelt, dropOrder, offLine, pitch
vars == <<chair, onBelt, dropOrder, offLine, pitch>>

Manned == chair.who # Unmanned

TypeOK ==
  /\ chair \in [who : Supervisors \cup {Unmanned}, term : 0 .. TermTop]
  /\ onBelt \subseteq Vehicles
  /\ dropOrder \in [Vehicles -> 0 .. TermTop]
  /\ offLine \subseteq Vehicles
  /\ pitch \in 0 .. ExitPitch

Init ==
  /\ chair = [who |-> Unmanned, term |-> 0]
  /\ onBelt = {}
  /\ dropOrder = [v \in Vehicles |-> 0]
  /\ offLine = {}
  /\ pitch = 0

\* Shift change, not a crash: the chair is stepped away from and picked up again
\* in a strictly higher term. Nobody in this shop ever stops responding.
StepAway ==
  /\ Manned
  /\ chair' = [chair EXCEPT !.who = Unmanned]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onBelt, dropOrder, offLine, pitch>>

TakeChair(g) ==
  /\ chair.term < TermTop
  /\ chair.who # g
  /\ chair' = [who |-> g, term |-> chair.term + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onBelt, dropOrder, offLine, pitch>>

\* A vehicle that has already been let out onto the road never comes back.
LoadOn(v) ==
  /\ v \notin onBelt
  /\ v \notin offLine
  /\ Cardinality(onBelt) < LineCap
  /\ onBelt' = onBelt \cup {v}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<chair, dropOrder, offLine, pitch>>

\* Only the supervisor in the chair writes a drop order, and only for a vehicle
\* that has no standing order yet; the order is stamped with the chair's term.
WriteOrder(v) ==
  /\ Manned
  /\ v \in onBelt
  /\ dropOrder[v] = 0
  /\ dropOrder' = [dropOrder EXCEPT ![v] = chair.term]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<chair, onBelt, offLine, pitch>>

TurnChain ==
  /\ pitch' = (pitch + 1) % BeltPitches
  /\ UNCHANGED <<chair, onBelt, dropOrder, offLine>>

\* The irreversible step: the gate opens and the vehicle leaves onto the public
\* road. The gate crew is slow -- it only acts when the chain reaches the exit
\* pitch -- but it never stops working, and it takes the car off the belt in the
\* same step, which is why no later order can let the same car out twice.
OpenGate(v) ==
  /\ pitch = ExitPitch
  /\ v \in onBelt
  /\ dropOrder[v] # 0
  /\ onBelt' = onBelt \ {v}
  /\ offLine' = offLine \cup {v}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<chair, dropOrder, pitch>>

Next ==
  \/ StepAway
  \/ \E g \in Supervisors : TakeChair(g)
  \/ \E v \in Vehicles : LoadOn(v)
  \/ \E v \in Vehicles : WriteOrder(v)
  \/ TurnChain
  \/ \E v \in Vehicles : OpenGate(v)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(TurnChain)
  /\ SF_vars(\E v \in Vehicles : OpenGate(v))

\* Every vehicle out on the road left under a standing drop order and is gone
\* from the belt, so the one irreversible release can never be repeated for it.
ReleasedCarsLeftUnderOrder ==
  \A v \in Vehicles :
    v \in offLine => (v \notin onBelt /\ dropOrder[v] # 0)

\* The gate crew is slow, never absent: a standing order always gets worked.
EveryOrderedVehicleEventuallyLeaves ==
  \A v \in Vehicles :
    (v \in onBelt /\ dropOrder[v] # 0) ~> (v \in offLine)
============================================================================

Nobody in this shop ever stops responding -- the gate crew in particular is slow, not absent.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m3p5t4 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Matchers, Symbols, Prices, NoPrice, Nobody, TermTop, DepthChoices

VARIABLES reign, book, tape, depth, queued
vars == <<reign, book, tape, depth, queued>>

InChair == reign.who # Nobody

TypeOK ==
  /\ reign \in [who : Matchers \cup {Nobody}, term : 0 .. TermTop]
  /\ book \in [Symbols -> Prices \cup {NoPrice}]
  /\ tape \in [Symbols -> Prices \cup {NoPrice}]
  /\ depth \in DepthChoices
  /\ queued \in [Symbols -> 0 .. 2]

Init ==
  /\ reign = [who |-> Nobody, term |-> 0]
  /\ book = [s \in Symbols |-> NoPrice]
  /\ tape = [s \in Symbols |-> NoPrice]
  /\ depth = 1
  /\ queued = [s \in Symbols |-> 0]

\* Failover of the matching engine: the chair empties and is retaken in a
\* strictly higher term. Nothing already on the tape depends on who holds it.
Yield ==
  /\ InChair
  /\ reign' = [reign EXCEPT !.who = Nobody]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<book, tape, depth, queued>>

Claim(m) ==
  /\ reign.term < TermTop
  /\ reign.who # m
  /\ reign' = [who |-> m, term |-> reign.term + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<book, tape, depth, queued>>

\* Order book depth is re-declared while the auction runs; it may never be set
\* below what is already resting on any symbol.
Redepth(k) ==
  /\ \A s \in Symbols : queued[s] <= k
  /\ depth' = k
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reign, book, tape, queued>>

Quote(s) ==
  /\ queued[s] < depth
  /\ queued' = [queued EXCEPT ![s] = queued[s] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reign, book, tape, depth>>

\* The chair seals the indicative cross for a symbol. A symbol whose print is
\* already on the tape can never have its cross re-sealed at another price.
SealCross(s, p) ==
  /\ InChair
  /\ book[s] = NoPrice
  /\ tape[s] = NoPrice
  /\ queued[s] > 0
  /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![s] = p]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reign, tape, depth, queued>>

\* The irreversible step: the opening print goes out on the public tape.
PrintOpen(s) ==
  /\ InChair
  /\ book[s] # NoPrice
  /\ tape[s] = NoPrice
  /\ tape' = [tape EXCEPT ![s] = book[s]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reign, book, depth, queued>>

Next ==
  \/ Yield
  \/ \E m \in Matchers : Claim(m)
  \/ \E k \in DepthChoices : Redepth(k)
  \/ \E s \in Symbols : Quote(s)
  \/ \E s \in Symbols, p \in Prices : SealCross(s, p)
  \/ \E s \in Symbols : PrintOpen(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Once a symbol's opening print is on the tape it still matches the cross that
\* was sealed for it, so no failover chair can rewrite that one printed price.
PrintedOpenIsImmutable ==
  \A s \in Symbols : tape[s] # NoPrice => tape[s] = book[s]
===========================================================================
nl:
A stock exchange runs an opening auction for each of its symbols. The matching engine is run by whichever matcher currently holds the chair; the chair can empty at any moment and is retaken by a matcher in a strictly higher term, which is how the exchange fails over during the auction. A bounded number of terms is recorded per opening.

Orders rest on each symbol's book, and the exchange re-declares the permitted book depth while the auction is running as volatility bands are widened or tightened. A re-declaration may raise or lower the depth but may never set it below what is already resting on any symbol, and a new order may only be quoted onto a symbol while that symbol is below the current depth.

The chair seals the indicative cross for a symbol, choosing the price at which the auction will open, and it may only do so for a symbol that has orders resting, has no sealed cross yet, and has nothing on the tape yet. The irreversible step is the opening print: the sealed cross goes out on the public tape for that symbol, and a printed open cannot be withdrawn, amended or reprinted. Because a symbol whose print is already on the tape can never have its cross re-sealed, the printed price stays exactly the price that was sealed.

The full action set is: the chair is yielded, a matcher claims the chair in a higher term, the book depth is re-declared at runtime, an order is quoted onto a symbol below the current depth, the chair seals the indicative cross for a symbol, and the chair prints the opening on the public tape.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Once a symbol's opening print is on the public tape, it still matches the cross that was sealed for that symbol, so no failover of the chair can rewrite or repeat that one irreversible print.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m2p0t3 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Apps, Hubs, NoApp, Unpromised, ThrowCap

VARIABLES round, promise, control, bolt, throws
vars == <<round, promise, control, bolt, throws>>

AllPromised == \A h \in Hubs : promise[h] = round.suitor
SomeoneElsesHub == \E h \in Hubs : promise[h] # Unpromised /\ promise[h] # round.suitor

TypeOK ==
  /\ round \in [suitor : Apps \cup {NoApp}, phase : {"quiet", "polling"}]
  /\ promise \in [Hubs -> Apps \cup {Unpromised}]
  /\ control \in [Apps -> {"clear", "asking", "holding"}]
  /\ bolt \in {"thrown", "drawn"}
  /\ throws \in 0 .. ThrowCap

Init ==
  /\ round = [suitor |-> NoApp, phase |-> "quiet"]
  /\ promise = [h \in Hubs |-> Unpromised]
  /\ control = [a \in Apps |-> "clear"]
  /\ bolt = "drawn"
  /\ throws = 0

\* One round at a time: an app asks for the deadbolt and the coordinator starts
\* polling the hubs on its behalf.
Ask(a) ==
  /\ round.phase = "quiet"
  /\ control[a] = "clear"
  /\ round' = [suitor |-> a, phase |-> "polling"]
  /\ control' = [control EXCEPT ![a] = "asking"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<promise, bolt, throws>>

\* Hubs are slow, never dead: an unpromised hub answers the poll whenever it
\* gets round to it, promising itself to the suitor of the open round.
HubPromises(h) ==
  /\ round.phase = "polling"
  /\ promise[h] = Unpromised
  /\ promise' = [promise EXCEPT ![h] = round.suitor]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, control, bolt, throws>>

\* If any hub is already promised elsewhere the round cannot commit, so it is
\* rolled back and only this round's own promises are handed back.
Rebuff ==
  /\ round.phase = "polling"
  /\ SomeoneElsesHub
  /\ promise' = [h \in Hubs |->
        IF promise[h] = round.suitor THEN Unpromised ELSE promise[h]]
  /\ control' = [control EXCEPT ![round.suitor] = "clear"]
  /\ round' = [suitor |-> NoApp, phase |-> "quiet"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bolt, throws>>

Commit ==
  /\ round.phase = "polling"
  /\ AllPromised
  /\ control' = [control EXCEPT ![round.suitor] = "holding"]
  /\ round' = [suitor |-> NoApp, phase |-> "quiet"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<promise, bolt, throws>>

\* Only the app that carries every hub's promise may move the deadbolt.
MoveBolt(a) ==
  /\ control[a] = "holding"
  /\ throws < ThrowCap
  /\ bolt' = IF bolt = "drawn" THEN "thrown" ELSE "drawn"
  /\ throws' = throws + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, promise, control>>

HandBack(a) ==
  /\ control[a] = "holding"
  /\ control' = [control EXCEPT ![a] = "clear"]
  /\ promise' = [h \in Hubs |-> Unpromised]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, bolt, throws>>

Next ==
  \/ \E a \in Apps : Ask(a)
  \/ \E h \in Hubs : HubPromises(h)
  \/ Rebuff
  \/ Commit
  \/ \E a \in Apps : MoveBolt(a)
  \/ \E a \in Apps : HandBack(a)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(\E h \in Hubs : HubPromises(h))
  /\ WF_vars(Commit)
  /\ WF_vars(Rebuff)
  /\ WF_vars(\E a \in Apps : HandBack(a))

\* An app only has the deadbolt while every hub in the house is promised to it,
\* and a hub is promised to one app at a time, so control is never shared.
HolderCarriesEveryHubPromise ==
  \A a \in Apps :
    control[a] = "holding" => \A h \in Hubs : promise[h] = a

\* Control of the deadbolt is never kept forever; it always comes back.
EveryHoldIsEventuallyHandedBack ==
  \A a \in Apps : (control[a] = "holding") ~> (control[a] = "clear")
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Apps = {phone, keypad, watch}
    Hubs = {front, back, garage}
    NoApp = noapp
    Unpromised = unpromised
    ThrowCap = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT HolderCarriesEveryHubPromise

PROPERTY EveryHoldIsEventuallyHandedBack
nl:
A smart-home door lock network gives control of the front deadbolt to one app at a time. Control is agreed by a two-phase commit across the house's lock hubs, and the coordinator runs one round at a time.

A clear app asks for the deadbolt, which opens a round with that app as the suitor and starts polling the hubs. The hubs in this house are slow but never dead: an unpromised hub answers the poll whenever it gets round to it, promising itself to the suitor of the open round, and it may take a while about it. If any hub turns out to be already promised to somebody else, the round cannot commit: it is rolled back, the suitor goes back to clear, and only the promises made in this round are handed back, leaving the other app's promises alone. If every hub in the house is promised to the suitor, the round commits and the suitor takes control of the deadbolt.

Only the app holding control may move the deadbolt, throwing or drawing it, and the network logs a limited number of throws per session. An app holding control eventually hands it back, which returns every hub to unpromised so the next round can succeed.

The full action set is: a clear app asks for the deadbolt and opens a round, a slow hub promises itself to the open round's suitor, a round is rebuffed and rolled back when a hub is already promised elsewhere, a fully promised round commits and hands control to the suitor, the holder moves the deadbolt, and the holder hands control back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: An app only holds the deadbolt while every hub in the house is promised to it, and a hub is promised to at most one app at a time, so two apps can never both hold control of the deadbolt.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Control of the deadbolt is never kept forever -- every app that takes control eventually hands it back and releases the hubs.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od6m5p0t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cars, Controllers, Nobody, NoCar, ReconfigCap

VARIABLES panel, shaft, carMode, onDuty, reconfigs
vars == <<panel, shaft, carMode, onDuty, reconfigs>>

Backing(c) == {p \in onDuty : panel[p] = c}
Spare == {p \in onDuty : panel[p] = Nobody}
Majority(c) == 2 * Cardinality(Backing(c)) > Cardinality(onDuty)
Hopeless(c) == 2 * (Cardinality(Backing(c)) + Cardinality(Spare)) <= Cardinality(onDuty)

TypeOK ==
  /\ panel \in [Controllers -> Cars \cup {Nobody}]
  /\ shaft \in Cars \cup {NoCar}
  /\ carMode \in [Cars -> {"parked", "bidding", "express"}]
  /\ onDuty \subseteq Controllers
  /\ reconfigs \in 0 .. ReconfigCap

Init ==
  /\ panel = [p \in Controllers |-> Nobody]
  /\ shaft = NoCar
  /\ carMode = [c \in Cars |-> "parked"]
  /\ onDuty = Controllers
  /\ reconfigs = 0

Bid(c) ==
  /\ carMode[c] = "parked"
  /\ carMode' = [carMode EXCEPT ![c] = "bidding"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<panel, shaft, onDuty, reconfigs>>

\* An on-duty controller backs at most one bidding car at a time.
Back(p, c) ==
  /\ p \in onDuty
  /\ panel[p] = Nobody
  /\ carMode[c] = "bidding"
  /\ panel' = [panel EXCEPT ![p] = c]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shaft, carMode, onDuty, reconfigs>>

\* A car enters the express hoistway only on a strict majority of the on-duty
\* controllers; two such majorities always share a controller.
EnterShaft(c) ==
  /\ carMode[c] = "bidding"
  /\ Majority(c)
  /\ shaft = NoCar
  /\ shaft' = c
  /\ carMode' = [carMode EXCEPT ![c] = "express"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<panel, onDuty, reconfigs>>

StandDown(c) ==
  /\ carMode[c] = "bidding"
  /\ Hopeless(c)
  /\ carMode' = [carMode EXCEPT ![c] = "parked"]
  /\ panel' = [p \in Controllers |-> IF panel[p] = c THEN Nobody ELSE panel[p]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shaft, onDuty, reconfigs>>

ClearShaft(c) ==
  /\ carMode[c] = "express"
  /\ shaft = c
  /\ shaft' = NoCar
  /\ carMode' = [carMode EXCEPT ![c] = "parked"]
  /\ panel' = [p \in Controllers |-> IF panel[p] = c THEN Nobody ELSE panel[p]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onDuty, reconfigs>>

\* Controllers are taken out of service and put back while the bank runs, which
\* moves the majority threshold. It is only ever done with the hoistway empty
\* and no backing recorded, so no old majority can survive the change.
Restaff(s) ==
  /\ reconfigs < ReconfigCap
  /\ shaft = NoCar
  /\ \A p \in Controllers : panel[p] = Nobody
  /\ s # {}
  /\ s # onDuty
  /\ onDuty' = s
  /\ reconfigs' = reconfigs + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<panel, shaft, carMode>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Bid(c)
  \/ \E p \in Controllers, c \in Cars : Back(p, c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : EnterShaft(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : StandDown(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : ClearShaft(c)
  \/ \E s \in SUBSET Controllers : Restaff(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A car running the express hoistway is the car the hoistway is assigned to and
\* is carrying a strict majority of the controllers currently on duty.
ExpressCarHoldsOnDutyMajority ==
  \A c \in Cars :
    carMode[c] = "express" => (shaft = c /\ Majority(c))
============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Cars = {carA, carB}
    Controllers = {dc1, dc2, dc3}
    Nobody = nobody
    NoCar = nocar
    ReconfigCap = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT ExpressCarHoldsOnDutyMajority
nl:
A skyscraper's elevator bank has one express hoistway that runs straight to the sky lobby, and only one car may be in it at a time. Which car gets it is decided by quorum voting among the bank's dispatch controllers rather than by a single scheduler.

A parked car bids for the hoistway. Each controller that is on duty may back at most one bidding car at a time. A car that is backed by a strict majority of the controllers currently on duty enters the express hoistway, provided the hoistway is empty; since two strict majorities of the same on-duty set always share a controller, no two cars can both be backed by a majority. A bidding car whose backing plus the controllers still uncommitted could never add up to a majority stands down, releasing the backing recorded in its name. A car finishing its express run clears the hoistway and releases its backing.

Controller staffing changes while the bank is running: controllers are taken out of service for maintenance and put back, and this moves the majority threshold, because the threshold is always measured against the controllers currently on duty. Restaffing is only ever done with the hoistway empty and no backing recorded anywhere, so no majority collected under the old staffing can survive the change, and the building limits how many restaffings happen in a service window.

The full action set is: a parked car bids, an on-duty controller backs a bidding car, a majority-backed car enters the empty express hoistway, a car with no path to a majority stands down, a car clears the hoistway after its run, and the bank is restaffed with a different on-duty controller set.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any car running the express hoistway is the car the hoistway is assigned to and is carrying a strict majority of the controllers currently on duty, so two cars can never be in the express hoistway at the same time even as staffing moves the majority threshold.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m2p2t5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS FeederA, FeederB, FeederC, Blocks, FeederCap, DispatchedMW

Feeders == {FeederA, FeederB, FeederC}

VARIABLES load, escrow, shed, transfer, ayes
vars == <<load, escrow, shed, transfer, ayes>>

Carried == load[FeederA] + load[FeederB] + load[FeederC]

Parties == {transfer.from, transfer.to}
CanBack(f) ==
  IF f = transfer.to THEN load[f] + transfer.block <= FeederCap
                     ELSE load[f] >= transfer.block

TypeOK ==
  /\ load \in [Feeders -> 0 .. FeederCap]
  /\ escrow \in 0 .. DispatchedMW
  /\ shed \in 0 .. DispatchedMW
  /\ transfer \in [from : Feeders, to : Feeders, block : Blocks,
                   phase : {"idle", "voting", "settling"}]
  /\ ayes \subseteq Feeders

Init ==
  /\ load = [f \in Feeders |-> 1]
  /\ escrow = 0
  /\ shed = 0
  /\ transfer = [from |-> FeederA, to |-> FeederB, block |-> 1, phase |-> "idle"]
  /\ ayes = {}

OpenTransfer(a, b, m) ==
  /\ transfer.phase = "idle"
  /\ a # b
  /\ transfer' = [from |-> a, to |-> b, block |-> m, phase |-> "voting"]
  /\ ayes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<load, escrow, shed>>

\* Only the two feeders in the transfer vote, and each backs it only if its own
\* side of the move is feasible. Voting moves no megawatts at all.
CastAye(f) ==
  /\ transfer.phase = "voting"
  /\ f \in Parties
  /\ f \notin ayes
  /\ CanBack(f)
  /\ ayes' = ayes \cup {f}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<load, escrow, shed, transfer>>

Abandon ==
  /\ transfer.phase = "voting"
  /\ \E f \in Parties : f \notin ayes /\ ~CanBack(f)
  /\ transfer' = [transfer EXCEPT !.phase = "idle"]
  /\ ayes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<load, escrow, shed>>

\* Both aye votes in: the block leaves the sending feeder into escrow. It is in
\* escrow, not nowhere, which is what keeps the megawatt ledger balanced
\* between the two halves of the commit.
Escrow ==
  /\ transfer.phase = "voting"
  /\ ayes = Parties
  /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![transfer.from] = load[transfer.from] - transfer.block]
  /\ escrow' = escrow + transfer.block
  /\ transfer' = [transfer EXCEPT !.phase = "settling"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shed, ayes>>

Deliver ==
  /\ transfer.phase = "settling"
  /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![transfer.to] = load[transfer.to] + escrow]
  /\ escrow' = 0
  /\ transfer' = [transfer EXCEPT !.phase = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shed, ayes>>

\* Privileged override: the system operator sheds a block off a feeder without
\* asking anyone. The megawatts move to the shed register; none are destroyed.
OperatorShed(f, m) ==
  /\ load[f] >= m
  /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![f] = load[f] - m]
  /\ shed' = shed + m
  /\ UNCHANGED <<escrow, transfer, ayes>>

OperatorRestore(f, m) ==
  /\ shed >= m
  /\ load[f] + m <= FeederCap
  /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![f] = load[f] + m]
  /\ shed' = shed - m
  /\ UNCHANGED <<escrow, transfer, ayes>>

Next ==
  \/ \E a, b \in Feeders, m \in Blocks : OpenTransfer(a, b, m)
  \/ \E f \in Feeders : CastAye(f)
  \/ Abandon
  \/ Escrow
  \/ Deliver
  \/ \E f \in Feeders, m \in Blocks : OperatorShed(f, m)
  \/ \E f \in Feeders, m \in Blocks : OperatorRestore(f, m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every dispatched megawatt is somewhere the control room can point at: on a
\* feeder, held in transfer escrow, or on the shed register. The two-phase move
\* and the operator's override both only relocate megawatts, never mint them.
GridMegawattsAreConserved ==
  Carried + escrow + shed = DispatchedMW
============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    FeederA = fa
    FeederB = fb
    FeederC = fc
    Blocks = {1, 2}
    FeederCap = 3
    DispatchedMW = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT GridMegawattsAreConserved
nl:
A power-grid load shedder keeps track of every dispatched megawatt on the network. At any moment a megawatt is either being carried by one of the feeders, held in escrow in the middle of a transfer, or sitting on the shed register having been dropped. The control room must always be able to say where every dispatched megawatt is.

Moving a block of load from one feeder to another is done by a two-phase commit between exactly the two feeders involved. The control room opens a transfer naming the sending feeder, the receiving feeder and the block size. Each of the two feeders casts an aye only if its own side of the move is feasible -- the sender must actually be carrying the block, and the receiver must have room for it under its feeder cap. Voting moves no megawatts at all. If either feeder cannot back the transfer, the round is abandoned and again nothing moves. Once both ayes are in, the block leaves the sending feeder into transfer escrow, and the settling step then lands the escrowed block on the receiving feeder.

There is a privileged override. The system operator may shed a block straight off any feeder without asking anyone, which moves those megawatts onto the shed register, and may restore a shed block back onto any feeder that has room for it. The override bypasses the voting entirely but still only relocates megawatts.

The full action set is: the control room opens a transfer between two feeders, a feeder casts its aye when its side is feasible, an infeasible round is abandoned, a fully backed transfer moves the block into escrow, the escrowed block is delivered onto the receiving feeder, the operator sheds a block off a feeder under override, and the operator restores a shed block onto a feeder.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The megawatts carried on the feeders, the megawatts held in transfer escrow and the megawatts on the shed register always add up to exactly the dispatched total, so neither the two-phase transfer nor the operator's override ever creates or destroys load.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od16m8p5t2 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS ArmOne, ArmTwo, Scripts, Drawers, Nobody

Arms == {ArmOne, ArmTwo}

VARIABLES basket, inHand, labelledBy, cabinet, drawerKey
vars == <<basket, inHand, labelledBy, cabinet, drawerKey>>

HasScript(r) == \E s \in Scripts : inHand[s] = r
HasDrawer(r) == \E d \in Drawers : drawerKey[d] = r

TypeOK ==
  /\ basket \subseteq Scripts
  /\ inHand \in [Scripts -> Arms \cup {Nobody}]
  /\ labelledBy \in [Scripts -> Arms \cup {Nobody}]
  /\ cabinet \in Arms \cup {Nobody}
  /\ drawerKey \in [Drawers -> Arms \cup {Nobody}]

Init ==
  /\ basket = Scripts
  /\ inHand = [s \in Scripts |-> Nobody]
  /\ labelledBy = [s \in Scripts |-> Nobody]
  /\ cabinet = Nobody
  /\ drawerKey = [d \in Drawers |-> Nobody]

\* Two dispensing arms work the same basket of scripts and the same pool of
\* controlled-drug drawers; an arm carries one script at a time.
PickUp(r, s) ==
  /\ ~HasScript(r)
  /\ s \in basket
  /\ basket' = basket \ {s}
  /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![s] = r]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<labelledBy, cabinet, drawerKey>>

\* Coarse lock first: the cabinet key is taken before any drawer key, and only
\* by an arm that is not already holding a drawer.
TakeCabinet(r) ==
  /\ HasScript(r)
  /\ ~HasDrawer(r)
  /\ cabinet = Nobody
  /\ cabinet' = r
  /\ UNCHANGED <<basket, inHand, labelledBy, drawerKey>>

\* Fine lock second, and the coarse key is handed straight back as it is taken.
TakeDrawer(r, d) ==
  /\ cabinet = r
  /\ drawerKey[d] = Nobody
  /\ drawerKey' = [drawerKey EXCEPT ![d] = r]
  /\ cabinet' = Nobody
  /\ UNCHANGED <<basket, inHand, labelledBy>>

\* The irreversible step: the tamper seal is broken and the single-use label is
\* printed against the script. The script leaves the arm's hand in the same
\* step and can never be picked up out of the basket again.
PrintLabel(r, s, d) ==
  /\ inHand[s] = r
  /\ drawerKey[d] = r
  /\ labelledBy[s] = Nobody
  /\ labelledBy' = [labelledBy EXCEPT ![s] = r]
  /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![s] = Nobody]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<basket, cabinet, drawerKey>>

DropDrawer(r, d) ==
  /\ drawerKey[d] = r
  /\ ~HasScript(r)
  /\ drawerKey' = [drawerKey EXCEPT ![d] = Nobody]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<basket, inHand, labelledBy, cabinet>>

\* An empty-handed arm also uses the coarse key for routine stock checks, and
\* always hands it back, so it never blocks an arm that is carrying a script.
StockCheck(r) ==
  /\ ~HasScript(r)
  /\ cabinet = Nobody
  /\ cabinet' = r
  /\ UNCHANGED <<basket, inHand, labelledBy, drawerKey>>

EndCheck(r) ==
  /\ ~HasScript(r)
  /\ cabinet = r
  /\ cabinet' = Nobody
  /\ UNCHANGED <<basket, inHand, labelledBy, drawerKey>>

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Arms, s \in Scripts : PickUp(r, s)
  \/ \E r \in Arms : TakeCabinet(r)
  \/ \E r \in Arms, d \in Drawers : TakeDrawer(r, d)
  \/ \E r \in Arms, s \in Scripts, d \in Drawers : PrintLabel(r, s, d)
  \/ \E r \in Arms, d \in Drawers : DropDrawer(r, d)
  \/ \E r \in Arms : StockCheck(r)
  \/ \E r \in Arms : EndCheck(r)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ SF_vars(TakeCabinet(ArmOne))
  /\ SF_vars(TakeCabinet(ArmTwo))
  /\ WF_vars(\E d \in Drawers : TakeDrawer(ArmOne, d))
  /\ WF_vars(\E d \in Drawers : TakeDrawer(ArmTwo, d))
  /\ WF_vars(\E r \in Arms, s \in Scripts, d \in Drawers : PrintLabel(r, s, d))
  /\ WF_vars(\E r \in Arms, d \in Drawers : DropDrawer(r, d))
  /\ WF_vars(\E r \in Arms : EndCheck(r))

\* A script whose single-use label has been printed is out of the basket and out
\* of every arm's hand, so the irreversible print can never happen to it twice.
LabelledScriptsAreOutOfCirculation ==
  \A s \in Scripts :
    labelledBy[s] # Nobody => (s \notin basket /\ inHand[s] = Nobody)

\* An arm never keeps hold of a script: it always gets its locks and prints.
EveryHeldScriptEventuallyLabelled ==
  \A s \in Scripts : (inHand[s] # Nobody) ~> (labelledBy[s] # Nobody)
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    ArmOne = arm1
    ArmTwo = arm2
    Scripts = {rx1, rx2, rx3}
    Drawers = {dw1, dw2}
    Nobody = nobody

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT LabelledScriptsAreOutOfCirculation

PROPERTY EveryHeldScriptEventuallyLabelled
nl:
A pharmacy's prescription dispenser has two dispensing arms working as independent instances over one shared basket of scripts and one shared pool of controlled-drug drawers. An arm carries at most one script at a time, and picks a script up out of the shared basket.

Access to the drawers is hierarchical. An arm must first take the coarse cabinet key, and it may only do so while carrying a script and while holding no drawer key. Holding the cabinet key it then takes the fine key of a free drawer, handing the cabinet key straight back in the very same step so the other arm can start its own sequence.

The irreversible step is printing the label: the tamper seal on the vial is broken and the single-use label is printed against the script. An arm may only print while it is carrying that script and holding a drawer key. Printing takes the script out of the arm's hand in the same step, and a script that carries a printed label is never put back into the basket, so the seal can never be broken for it twice. An arm that is carrying no script drops its drawer key. An empty-handed arm also uses the coarse cabinet key for routine stock checks and always hands it back, so a stock check never blocks an arm that is carrying a script.

The full action set is: an arm picks a script up out of the shared basket, an arm takes the coarse cabinet key, an arm takes a fine drawer key and hands the cabinet key back, an arm prints the single-use label and breaks the seal, an empty-handed arm drops its drawer key, an empty-handed arm takes the cabinet key for a stock check, and an empty-handed arm hands the cabinet key back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every script whose single-use label has been printed is out of the shared basket and out of both arms' hands, so the irreversible seal-breaking print can never happen to the same script twice.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every script an arm has picked up is eventually labelled, so no script is carried around forever waiting on the cabinet and drawer keys.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od6m3p4t0 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Dispatchers, CarNorth, CarSouth, Vacant, CarCap, ShaftLimit, LobbyCap

Cars == {CarNorth, CarSouth}

VARIABLES aboard, pledged, chair, dark, lobby
vars == <<aboard, pledged, chair, dark, lobby>>

OnCar(c) == aboard[c] + pledged[c]
ShaftLoad == OnCar(CarNorth) + OnCar(CarSouth)

TypeOK ==
  /\ aboard \in [Cars -> 0 .. CarCap]
  /\ pledged \in [Cars -> 0 .. CarCap]
  /\ chair \in [who : Dispatchers \cup {Vacant}, term : 0 .. 2]
  /\ dark \subseteq Cars
  /\ lobby \in 0 .. LobbyCap

Init ==
  /\ aboard = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
  /\ pledged = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
  /\ chair = [who |-> Vacant, term |-> 0]
  /\ dark = {}
  /\ lobby = 0

TakeChair(d) ==
  /\ chair.term < 2
  /\ chair.who # d
  /\ chair' = [who |-> d, term |-> chair.term + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<aboard, pledged, dark, lobby>>

\* Failover: the chair simply empties and is taken again in a higher term.
ChairFails ==
  /\ chair.who # Vacant
  /\ chair' = [chair EXCEPT !.who = Vacant]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<aboard, pledged, dark, lobby>>

Arrive ==
  /\ lobby < LobbyCap
  /\ lobby' = lobby + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<aboard, pledged, chair, dark>>

\* A pledge counts against the shaft the moment the dispatcher makes it, before
\* anyone steps into the car, so both the car's own cap and the counterweight
\* limit for the whole shaft are checked against pledges as well as passengers.
Pledge(c) ==
  /\ chair.who # Vacant
  /\ lobby > 0
  /\ OnCar(c) < CarCap
  /\ ShaftLoad < ShaftLimit
  /\ pledged' = [pledged EXCEPT ![c] = pledged[c] + 1]
  /\ lobby' = lobby - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<aboard, chair, dark>>

Board(c) ==
  /\ c \notin dark
  /\ pledged[c] > 0
  /\ pledged' = [pledged EXCEPT ![c] = pledged[c] - 1]
  /\ aboard' = [aboard EXCEPT ![c] = aboard[c] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<chair, dark, lobby>>

Alight(c) ==
  /\ c \notin dark
  /\ aboard[c] > 0
  /\ aboard' = [aboard EXCEPT ![c] = aboard[c] - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pledged, chair, dark, lobby>>

\* A car controller can stop answering without telling anybody; its pledges
\* stay booked against the shaft until the dispatcher recalls them by hand.
GoDark(c) ==
  /\ c \notin dark
  /\ dark' = dark \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<aboard, pledged, chair, lobby>>

ComeBack(c) ==
  /\ c \in dark
  /\ dark' = dark \ {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<aboard, pledged, chair, lobby>>

Recall(c) ==
  /\ c \in dark
  /\ pledged[c] > 0
  /\ lobby < LobbyCap
  /\ pledged' = [pledged EXCEPT ![c] = pledged[c] - 1]
  /\ lobby' = lobby + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<aboard, chair, dark>>

Next ==
  \/ \E d \in Dispatchers : TakeChair(d)
  \/ ChairFails
  \/ Arrive
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Pledge(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Board(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Alight(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : GoDark(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : ComeBack(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Recall(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Passengers riding plus passengers pledged, summed over the whole bank, never
\* exceed the counterweight limit of the shaft -- not while the dispatcher chair
\* changes hands, and not while a car sits dark holding pledges nobody boarded.
ShaftLoadWithinCounterweight == ShaftLoad <= ShaftLimit
============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Dispatchers = {dp1, dp2}
    CarNorth = north
    CarSouth = south
    Vacant = vacant
    CarCap = 2
    ShaftLimit = 3
    LobbyCap = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT ShaftLoadWithinCounterweight
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper has two cars, north and south, sharing one hoistway. Each car has its own passenger cap, and the hoistway as a whole has a counterweight limit on how many passengers may be riding in the bank at once. Dispatching is run by whichever dispatcher process holds the chair; the chair can empty at any time and is then taken again by a dispatcher in a strictly higher term, which is how the bank fails over.

Passengers arrive into the lobby, up to the lobby's holding limit. The dispatcher pledges a waiting passenger to a car, and that pledge counts against the shaft from the moment it is made, before anyone has stepped into the car; so both the car's own cap and the counterweight limit for the whole bank are checked against pledges as well as against passengers already riding. A pledged passenger boards the car they were pledged to, and a riding passenger alights.

Car controllers are not reliable. A car controller can go dark without telling anybody -- nothing else changes and the dispatcher gets no notification -- and a dark car neither boards nor lands anybody, so its pledges stay booked against the shaft until the dispatcher recalls them by hand and puts those passengers back in the lobby. A dark controller may later come back into service.

The full action set is: a dispatcher takes the chair in a higher term, the chair fails and empties, a passenger arrives in the lobby, the dispatcher pledges a lobby passenger to a car, a pledged passenger boards, a riding passenger alights, a car controller goes dark, a dark controller comes back, and the dispatcher recalls a dark car's pledge back to the lobby.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The passengers riding plus the passengers pledged, summed over both cars, never exceed the hoistway's counterweight limit -- not while the dispatcher chair changes hands, and not while a car sits dark holding pledges that nobody ever boarded.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m6p6t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS RoboOne, RoboTwo, Aisles, Nobody, NoAisle, EpochSpan, LeaseTicks,
          StockCap, DockCap

Robots == {RoboOne, RoboTwo}
Epochs == 0 .. (EpochSpan - 1)
Blank == [aisle |-> NoAisle, epoch |-> 0]

VARIABLES lease, claim, stock, dock, bounced
vars == <<lease, claim, stock, dock, bounced>>

Alive(a) == lease[a].ttl > 0
Entitled(r) ==
  /\ claim[r].aisle # NoAisle
  /\ lease[claim[r].aisle].holder = r
  /\ lease[claim[r].aisle].epoch = claim[r].epoch
  /\ Alive(claim[r].aisle)

TypeOK ==
  /\ lease \in [Aisles -> [holder : Robots \cup {Nobody}, epoch : Epochs,
                           ttl : 0 .. LeaseTicks]]
  /\ claim \in [Robots -> [aisle : Aisles \cup {NoAisle}, epoch : Epochs]]
  /\ stock \in [Aisles -> 0 .. StockCap]
  /\ dock \in 0 .. DockCap
  /\ bounced \subseteq Robots

Init ==
  /\ lease = [a \in Aisles |-> [holder |-> Nobody, epoch |-> 0, ttl |-> 0]]
  /\ claim = [r \in Robots |-> Blank]
  /\ stock = [a \in Aisles |-> 0]
  /\ dock = DockCap
  /\ bounced = {}

\* Leases only run down; nothing renews one in place.
Tick ==
  /\ \E a \in Aisles : Alive(a)
  /\ lease' = [a \in Aisles |->
        IF Alive(a) THEN [lease[a] EXCEPT !.ttl = lease[a].ttl - 1] ELSE lease[a]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<claim, stock, dock, bounced>>

\* Epoch numbers come from a small recycled ring, so cutting a lease also tears
\* up any standing claim already carrying the epoch about to be reused.
CutLease(a, r) ==
  /\ ~Alive(a)
  /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![a] =
        [holder |-> r, epoch |-> (lease[a].epoch + 1) % EpochSpan,
         ttl |-> LeaseTicks]]
  /\ claim' = [q \in Robots |->
        IF claim[q].aisle = a /\ claim[q].epoch = (lease[a].epoch + 1) % EpochSpan
          THEN Blank ELSE claim[q]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, dock, bounced>>

\* Robots are slow, not broken: one picks up its lease whenever it gets round
\* to it, and it records the epoch it was told about.
PickUpClaim(r, a) ==
  /\ claim[r].aisle = NoAisle
  /\ lease[a].holder = r
  /\ Alive(a)
  /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![r] = [aisle |-> a, epoch |-> lease[a].epoch]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, stock, dock, bounced>>

\* A pallet is only put away by a robot whose standing claim still matches the
\* aisle's live lease, epoch and all.
PutAway(r) ==
  /\ Entitled(r)
  /\ dock > 0
  /\ stock[claim[r].aisle] < StockCap
  /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![claim[r].aisle] = stock[claim[r].aisle] + 1]
  /\ dock' = dock - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, claim, bounced>>

\* The floor controller turns away a robot whose claim no longer matches, and
\* the robot drops the claim. This is how a slow robot finds out it is stale.
BounceStale(r) ==
  /\ claim[r].aisle # NoAisle
  /\ ~Entitled(r)
  /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![r] = Blank]
  /\ bounced' = bounced \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, stock, dock>>

Retrieve(a) ==
  /\ stock[a] > 0
  /\ dock < DockCap
  /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![a] = stock[a] - 1]
  /\ dock' = dock + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, claim, bounced>>

Next ==
  \/ Tick
  \/ \E a \in Aisles, r \in Robots : CutLease(a, r)
  \/ \E r \in Robots, a \in Aisles : PickUpClaim(r, a)
  \/ \E r \in Robots : PutAway(r)
  \/ \E r \in Robots : BounceStale(r)
  \/ \E a \in Aisles : Retrieve(a)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(Tick)
  /\ WF_vars(BounceStale(RoboOne))
  /\ WF_vars(BounceStale(RoboTwo))

\* A standing claim that still reads as the aisle's current epoch really does
\* belong to the robot holding it; a robot left over from an earlier lease can
\* never look current to the floor controller.
NoStaleClaimLooksCurrent ==
  \A r \in Robots :
    (claim[r].aisle # NoAisle /\ claim[r].epoch = lease[claim[r].aisle].epoch)
      => lease[claim[r].aisle].holder = r

\* Slow robots still let go: a standing claim is always eventually dropped.
EveryClaimIsEventuallyDropped ==
  \A r \in Robots : (claim[r].aisle # NoAisle) ~> (claim[r].aisle = NoAisle)
============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    RoboOne = rb1
    RoboTwo = rb2
    Aisles = {ai1, ai2}
    Nobody = nobody
    NoAisle = noaisle
    EpochSpan = 2
    LeaseTicks = 1
    StockCap = 1
    DockCap = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoStaleClaimLooksCurrent

PROPERTY EveryClaimIsEventuallyDropped
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet works a set of aisles under leases. The floor controller cuts a lease on an aisle to one robot, for a fixed number of ticks, and leases only ever run down -- nothing renews a lease in place, and a new lease may only be cut on an aisle whose old lease has already run out. Each lease carries an epoch number drawn from a small recycled ring, so when the controller cuts a lease it also tears up any standing claim that already carries the epoch it is about to reuse.

The robots are slow but never broken. A robot with no standing claim picks its lease up whenever it gets round to it, recording the aisle and the epoch it was told about, and it may be well behind the floor by then. A pallet is only put away into an aisle by a robot whose standing claim still matches that aisle's live lease -- same holder, same epoch, lease not run out -- taking the pallet off the inbound dock. The floor controller turns away any robot whose claim no longer matches, and that robot drops its claim and is logged as bounced; this is how a slow robot finds out it has gone stale. Pallets are also retrieved back out of an aisle to the dock.

The full action set is: a tick runs live leases down, the controller cuts a fresh lease on an expired aisle and tears up claims carrying the reused epoch, a slow robot picks up its standing claim, an entitled robot puts a pallet away into its aisle, the controller bounces a robot whose claim no longer matches, and a pallet is retrieved from an aisle back to the dock.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any standing claim that still reads as its aisle's current epoch really does belong to the robot holding it, so a robot left over from an earlier lease can never look current to the floor controller and act on the aisle.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every standing claim a robot picks up is eventually dropped, so no slow robot sits on a claim forever.
